General Motors recently announced plans to prepare its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant in Michigan for hybrid vehicle production, signaling a shift from its heavy focus on EVs. While the move could help the automaker better navigate the U.S. market in the years ahead, the plant has a more immediate problem to address: six vehicles it produced are being recalled over improperly welded seats.

The affected vehicles include three MY2026 GMC Acadias and three MY2026 Chevrolet Traverses. Four vehicles are being recalled in the U.S. under NHTSA recall number 26V696, while the remaining two are covered by a recall in Canada. Because the front seats in these vehicles may be improperly welded, they might not provide adequate support during a crash, increasing the risk of injury, even when occupants are wearing seatbelts.

According to NHTSA, the defect was discovered after the driver’s seatback frame in a 2026 Chevy Traverse was replaced in July 2026. GM’s supplier subsequently reviewed laser-welding data from more than 94,000 seat components and identified six additional suspect parts, all manufactured on November 3, 2025. The problem stemmed from insufficient welds, also known as cold welds.

The safety agency noted that GM is not aware of any accidents or injuries related to the issue. The supplier has since revised its maintenance schedule and improved its weld inspection procedures to prevent similar defects from occurring.

As part of the remedy, affected owners will be advised to take their three-row midsize crossovers to dealerships for a seatback frame replacement, free of charge. Some affected vehicles have the problem with the driver’s seat, while others have it with the front passenger seat. NHTSA said that all covered vehicles are still under warranty, so a separate reimbursement program will not be offered.

GM will begin notifying affected U.S. owners on December 7, while VINs are already searchable in the recall database.

The Traverse and Acadia share GM’s C1 platform with the Buick Enclave, and all three are powered by a 2.5-liter turbocharged inline-four producing 328 horsepower and 326 lb-ft of torque. With all three crossovers built at Lansing Delta Township Assembly, the plant’s upcoming shift toward hybrid production raises the possibility that these nameplates could be among the first to receive hybrid powertrains. However, the automaker has yet to confirm which models will be electrified first, leaving the Chevrolet Corvette as its sole hybrid offering stateside.

#4468. Waymo picks Toyota bZ4X as its next robotaxi, starting in Japan in 2027

Waymo is adding the Toyota bZ4X to its robotaxi lineup. Toyota will build a custom version of the electric SUV with the Waymo Driver integrated right on the line in Japan, and a test fleet will start operating there in 2027.

It’s the first actual vehicle to come out of the partnership the two companies signed last year. And it gives Waymo a Japanese-built car for its Tokyo launch, with the UK and other markets to follow.

When Waymo and Toyota first announced their deal in April 2025, it was a preliminary agreement to “explore” working together on autonomous driving, including in personally owned vehicles. Lots of intent, no product.

Now there’s a product. According to Waymo’s announcement, Toyota will produce the vehicles at its Takaoka plant in Toyota City, Aichi Prefecture, and Waymo’s self-driving hardware will be installed and integrated at that same site instead of being retrofitted somewhere else.

The robotaxi bZ4X gets a few rider-focused changes: extra rear legroom, automatic doors, a power liftgate, and ambient lighting. Waymo didn’t share sensor specs, unit volumes, or what each vehicle costs.

Operations in 2027 are about testing and validating the autonomous bZ4X fleet in Japan. The UK and “other Waymo markets” come in later years, with no dates attached.

The two companies also say they’ll keep working on autonomous tech for Toyota’s personal vehicles, plus safety projects with Woven by Toyota, the automaker’s software arm.

Waymo co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov said that “Toyota’s commitment to zero traffic accidents resonates deeply with us at Waymo.”

The timing lines up with Waymo’s Japan plans. In September, Waymo said it’s targeting fully driverless commercial rides in Tokyo in 2027 with taxi operator Nihon Kotsu and ride-hailing app GO, scaling to about 100 vehicles, pending regulatory approval.

In the US, Waymo’s fleet is still mostly made up of Jaguar I-Pace SUVs, a model Jaguar no longer produces. It’s been adding the Zeekr-built Ojai van and the Hyundai Ioniq 5, and Hyundai is reportedly in talks to supply up to 50,000 Ioniq 5 robotaxis by 2028.

The bZ4X makes four. It isn’t Toyota’s first robotaxi bZ4X either: Toyota and Pony.ai started mass-producing bZ4X-based robotaxis in China earlier this year.

For US readers, the refreshed model is sold here simply as the Toyota bZ, starting at $34,900. A cheap, high-volume base vehicle matters a lot when you’re trying to scale a fleet.

And Waymo is scaling. It now does over 500,000 paid rides a week across 15 US metros, and it picked Toronto as its first Canadian city earlier this month, with riders targeted for 2028.

This is a big one, even if the bZ4X is about as exciting as a toaster.

Waymo’s biggest constraint right now is cars. It has been running a fleet built on a discontinued Jaguar, and every new automaker it signs adds manufacturing capacity it doesn’t have to build itself. Toyota is the world’s best-selling automaker. Having it build Waymo-ready vehicles on its own assembly line is exactly the kind of industrial partner Waymo needed.

If Toyota and Waymo keep mentioning a personal vehicle, they are likely working on it. It doesn’t mean that it is going to happen but it’s obviously an avenue that they are both willing to explore. If things work out and they are actually able to bring a fully autonomous vehicle to market, that’s an extremely significant advantage from a top legacy car manufacturer that ultimately changes the game for Toyota and could potentially put them in the middle of the competition with other EV manufacturers.

Yes, the bZ4X had a rough start (Toyota recalled the first batch in 2022 because the wheels could come off). But it has come a long way now – becoming boring and reliable. And for a robotaxi, boring and reliable is the whole point.

Compare that with Tesla’s approach: a two-seat Cybercab with no steering wheel, built in-house, with a self-certified autonomy stack that still isn’t operating at anything close to Waymo’s scale. Waymo keeps plugging its driver into existing EVs from established automakers and expanding city by city. So far, that’s working.

The way it is looking now. It sounds like Toyota will take over manufacturing Waymo driver cars for right-hand-drive markets. But what interests me most is the personal-vehicle angle. Toyota and Waymo keep mentioning it, but there’s still nothing concrete. If Toyota actually puts the Waymo Driver in a car you can buy, Tesla’s FSD Supervised pitch gets a lot harder to sell. Will that happen before the end of the decade? Who knows.

The Lamborghini Gallardo is still one of the most instantly recognizable shapes to ever roll out of Sant’Agata Bolognese. When it landed in the early 2000s, it gave Lamborghini a real shot at the modern supercar game, offering a more approachable, slightly less wallet-destroying alternative to the big, bad Murciélago. With its screaming naturally aspirated V10, razor-sharp looks, and compact stance, the Gallardo basically became the poster car for a whole generation of gearheads.

Now, almost thirty years after first dreaming up the Gallardo, its original creator is back for another spin. Meet the HOMMAGE 26, a full-blown reimagining cooked up by CAVËN Atelier and led by none other than Fabrizio Giugiaro through his GFG Style studio.

Giugiaro first penned the Gallardo at Italdesign back in 1998, but this time he gets to go wild – no pesky production rules or bean counters holding him back. HOMMAGE 26 also kicks off CAVËN Atelier’s Designer Series, which basically lets legendary designers go back and remix their own icons.

The HOMMAGE 26 keeps some of that classic Gallardo DNA, especially up front. Giugiaro says the nose is pretty much straight from his 1998 vision, but the rear? That’s a whole new story. The end result is a mashup of old-school cues and modern touches, not some Frankenstein that forgets where it came from.

Surprisingly, barely anything from the original car survives. Only five parts make the cut: the roof, side windows, windshield, side mirrors, and their bases. Everything else? Brand new, including that slick carbon-fiber body.

Other wild touches include pop-down headlights (yes, down), active aero flaps, and a rear window you can actually open to show off the engine. These tweaks give the Gallardo a fresh vibe but keep its unmistakable silhouette intact.

CAVËN Atelier says the interior is getting a rethink too, but they’re keeping the details under wraps for now. Giugiaro calls the whole thing an evolution of an old idea, with some bits staying true to the past and others dragged into the present.

The mechanical side is just as spicy. The original 5.0-liter V10 sticks around, but Italtecnica has massaged it for more grunt. Now it screams up to 8,500 rpm and, yes, you get to row your own gears.

Buyers get two flavors: the GT with 540 horsepower, or the Performance version that bumps it up to 560. The chassis gets a two-mode suspension (comfort or sport), beefier brakes, and 20-inch wheels to round things out.

Only 25 HOMMAGE 26s will ever exist, each built from a first-gen Gallardo. You can bring your own donor car or let CAVËN Atelier hunt one down for you. The price? €900,000 (about $1 million at current exchange rates), and that’s before you even factor in the donor car or any extras. At least you’ll get dibs on whatever wild project comes next in the Designer Series.

#4466. Volkswagen hits pause on the Golf EV as it faces an ‘urgent need for action’

Volkswagen has put the electric Golf on hold for now as it faces growing pressure to cut costs.

“We cannot afford to lose any time and must act quickly and decisively,” Volkswagen Group CFO and COO Arno Antlitz warned after the company reported its largest quarterly loss since the “Dieselgate” scandal in 2015 on Thursday.

VW Group’s operating loss swelled to €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter because of a write-down of its Porsche stake, weak sales in China, and lower profit margins on electric vehicles.

As part of its latest cost-control efforts, Volkswagen is pausing development of the all-electric Golf at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.

“We simply can’t afford this work right now,” VW brand CEO Thomas Schäfer said in an internal memo Reuters reviewed on Friday. The Wolfsburg plant, or the “heart of the VW brand,” is about €300 million ($334.5 million) short of its cost-cutting targets, the memo said.

Schäfer said the “decision was really not an easy one for us,” knowing what the Golf means to Wolfsburg.

The decision comes after Volkswagen’s Supervisory Board approved its restructuring strategy, “Future Plan 2030,” last month, which includes reducing its global workforce by 100,000, trimming its lineup, and closing several plants in Germany.

Volkswagen initially planned to launch the Golf EV in 2028, but Schäfer confirmed earlier this year that the electric hatch will be delayed until closer to 2030.

It should be noted that they paid out dividends of 2.6 billion in August. Most of it went to 3 majority shareholders. But they used a clever accounting trick to delay the losses till now, just before talks with unions about pay.

Schäfer suggested the delay was because the SSP (Scalable Systems Platform), developed through its partnership with Rivian, was taking longer than expected.

The electric Golf, which is expected to arrive as the ID. Golf, will be one of the first vehicles based on the new platform.

While development is on hold, VW’s works council said the pause will not delay the Golf EV’s launch, promising to make up for lost time. It’s still expected to launch in 2030.

Volkswagen will begin building the electric Golf in Wolfsburg closer to the end of the decade, while production of the gas-powered model will move to Mexico in 2027.

#4464. Hyundai launches the new IONIQ 6 in the UK with up to 422 miles of range, starting at $45K

The new Hyundai IONIQ 6 is now on sale in the UK with an impressive range of up to 422 miles, starting at about $45,000.

Hyundai opened orders for the all-new IONIQ 6 in the UK, starting at £33,240 ($45,000), including the Electric Car Grant (ECG).

The “evolved” electrified streamliner brings a sharp new design, a refined interior, and a bigger battery for longer range.

Hyundai “enhanced every line and detail” for a cleaner, stronger silhouette. The front includes a redesigned shark nose and slim daytime running lights, while the black lower body garnish now extends into the doors.

The rear features a new extended ducktail design replacing the previous generation’s prominent spoiler.

Inside, Hyundai overhauled the new IONIQ 6’s interior with a redesigned two-tone leather steering wheel, a digital side mirror, and a “bridge-type” center console that includes a wireless phone charger and physical buttons.

It includes Hyundai’s new infotainment setup, including dual 12.3″ navigation and infotainment screens with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto capabilities.

In the UK, the new IONIQ 6 is available in three trims: Premium, N-Line, and N-Line Evo, with 225 horsepower RWD or 320 horsepower AWD powertrains.

The base Hyundai IONIQ 6 Premium uses a new 84 kWh battery with the 225 hp RWD powertrain, delivering up to 422 miles of range and 4.6 miles/kWh efficiency.

It starts at £33,240 with the ECG. It includes 18″ alloy wheels, flush auto door handles, dual-zone climate control, heated front seats, heated steering wheel, heat pump, smart regenerative braking, wireless phone charging, over-the-air updates, and the full suite of key safety systems.

The IONIQ 6 N-Line starts at £36,240, including the ECG, and adds a more dynamic N-Line exterior and interior design.

Upgrading to the range-topping N-Line Evo costs £43,270 and adds features like leather and suede seat trim, a suede headliner, front relaxation seats, ventilated front seats, an electric sunroof, and a head-up display.

Other added features included with the N-Line Evo trim include Surround View Monitor, Remote Smart Parking Assist, Parking Collision Avoidance Assist, Digital Key 2, Walk-Away Lock, exterior Vehicle-to-Load adaptor, and BOSE premium audio.

Both the IONIQ 6 N-Line and N-Line Evo use the 84 kWh battery, providing up to 364 miles of driving range in RWD and up to 354 miles with the AWD powertrain.

Beautiful car, very efficient and from what I read, very comfortable. I had my eyes set on it, but the small trunk was a dealbreaker for me. So I went for the EV6, which is maybe even more of a stunner (in the eyes of the beholder) but admittedly significantly less efficient.

Thanks to its 800-volt electrical architecture, the IONIQ 6’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in about 18 minutes at DC fast-charging speeds of up to 350 kW.

The new IONIQ 6 is now available to order on Hyundai UK’s website, with deliveries set to begin in early 2027.

Sadly, those in the US will miss out on the new-and-improved electrified streamliner. Hyundai is discontinuing the standard IONIQ 6 in the US after the 2026 model year, while the performance N will remain on sale.

Given the slowing demand for electric vehicles in the U.S., it comes as no surprise that Honda canceled three EVs planned for North America. The brand’s first mass-market EV in the region, the Prologue, is also being discontinued after just over two years on the market. Among the canceled models was the 0 SUV, which was intended to rival the Tesla Model Y. However, a newly granted U.S. design patent appears to bring the canceled SUV back to life, at least on paper.

The patent, first spotted by CarMoses, includes several drawings depicting what appears to be the 0 SUV prototype from different angles. The prototype was unveiled at CES 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada, alongside the 0 Saloon prototype. Both were later canceled, along with the Acura RSX, completing the trio of EVs that never made it to production.

Looking at the patent drawings, the side profile closely matches that of the 0 SUV prototype, particularly the rear quarter window between the C- and D-pillars. This design element is absent from the 0 Alpha, the smallest model unveiled in the 0 Series lineup. The 0 Alpha also features rear door handles integrated into the C-pillars, similar to the Honda HR-V and Toyota C-HR, helping create a coupe-like appearance. In contrast, the patent drawings show conventionally positioned door handles, matching those of the 0 SUV prototype.

The pixel-like headlights of the 0 SUV prototype also appear to be reflected in the patent drawings. Another matching design element is the front bumper, which features a prominent horizontal black trim piece and a sportier appearance than the one on the 0 Alpha.

Apart from those details, the patent could resemble either the 0 SUV or 0 Alpha prototype. Both share a similar boxy shape with a sloping roofline and pronounced wheel arches. Mentioning the 0 Alpha here is relevant, given that Honda hasn’t canceled it. However, it is primarily intended for Japan and India.

But again, these comparisons are based on visual cues only, so nothing is confirmed. Automakers often patent vehicle designs to protect their styling from competitors or preserve them for future use. After all, quirky, boxy shapes seem to be the go-to these days, as seen with the latest generations of the Hyundai Santa Fe and Lexus GX.

Honda’s focus in North America is now shifting toward hybrids, including the next-generation CR-V Hybrid, whose production was reportedly delayed by about three months to April 2027. The automaker plans to introduce 15 next-gen hybrid models globally by 2030, primarily targeting North America.

#4462. Toyota reveals five new lifted Woodland concepts, including the bZ electric SUV

Toyota introduced a new family of lifted, “adventure-ready” Woodland concepts based on the RAV4, Grand Highlander, Sienna, Crown Signia, and bZ electric SUV.

Toyota is the latest automaker to chase the highly profitable off-road market in the US, with plans to expand its “Woodland” lineup.

Although it already sells Woodland versions of the RAV4, Sienna, bZ, and most recently, the Grand Highlander, Toyota said the new family of concept vehicles is “designed for drivers who see adventure not as a destination, but a way of life.”

Toyota’s North American design studio, CALTY Design Research, designed the concepts to explore how some of its most popular nameplates can be used better on and off the road.

Each vehicle features Horizon Blue exterior paint, inspired by Toyota’s 1960s models, including the Stout, Crown, and Corona.

All new concepts also include an exclusive Woodland badge, plus a lift kit, large over-fenders, satin-black wheels, All-Terrain tires, two-tone paint on the roof and hood, a roof rack, and cross bars to top it off.

According to Toyota, the RAV4 Woodland Plug-In Hybrid and Sienna Woodland Concepts show how its “electrified and family-focused vehicles take on a more adventurous role.”

The electric Woodland bZ Concept “extends the Woodland theme into Toyota’s battery electric future.” Meanwhile, the Grand Highlander Woodland Concept and Crown Signia Woodland Concept bring two distinct models to the lineup, Toyota said.

The company didn’t reveal any powertrain specs or other details, but said the concepts show how capability can take many forms, including PHEV, hybrid, and battery electric.

Toyota’s new Woodland Concepts will be on display at the 2026 SEMA Show, starting on November 3.

To give you an idea, the 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland comes standard with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain, delivering a combined 375 horsepower. That’s an extra 37 hp compared to the standard bZ with AWD.

And for a mere 10-15% reduction in efficiency, our beautiful American suburbanites can Look Butch as they drive about town. Hopefully Toyota offers a package that attaches a shovel and some jerry cans to complete the image.

The bZ Woodland also adds off-road capabilities with 8.3″ of ground clearance and the ability to tow up to 3,500 lbs.

Other rugged upgrades include All-Terrain tires, black side molding, roof rails, and black wheel arch cladding.

The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380, or over $10,000 more than the standard bZ.

#4461. These Are Our Top-Rated Car Brands, Ranked

We averaged the individual ratings of the hundreds of models on sale to determine which brands are top-rated overall in our evaluations.

Which brands make the best cars? It's an age-old question that's constantly changing as car companies compete with each other to produce the latest and greatest products. But it's a question that we set out to answer with our comprehensive testing of every new vehicle we can get our hands on. We rate vehicle models on a one-to-10 scale—find more about how we determine our ratings here—and now we've averaged all our ratings by brand to determine which ones earn the highest ratings in Car and Driver's testing. We included the top 10 brands in this list.

Because we rate vehicles within their relative segments, this ranking of car brands shows which makes produce the most competitive products across the industry. These ratings come from a combination of objective instrumented testing and subjective real-world driving experience. And note that our ratings are constantly changing as we evaluate new products, so these average scores merely represent a snapshot of where these brands stand in today's evaluations.

Lucid is a new electric automaker that only started selling cars a few years ago, but it's off to a strong start. Both the Lucid Air electric luxury sedan and Lucid Gravity electric luxury SUV are previous winners of our 10Best award, so it's no surprise they rate highly in our book.

Porsche's lineup used to consist of only sports cars, but it has expanded in the past few decades to include SUVs, sedans, and several electric models. With the 911 sports car serving as the cornerstone of Porsche's excellent driving dynamics, the brand does a good job infusing the same precise feel into its other products, so nearly all Porsche models carry high C/D ratings.

Rivian, like Lucid, is a new EV automaker that has only a few models in its stable. But they're all good at what they do, so it's one of our top-rated brands. The R1S SUV and R1T pickup truck are Rivian's larger offerings, and the R2 compact SUV arrived recently to bring the brand's entry price point down to a more accessible level.

Another relatively new brand that quickly rose to the upper echlons of the automotive world is Genesis, Hyundai's luxury spinoff. It's been around since 2015, and its products have improved rapidly. The GV70 and GV80 luxury SUVs both sit near the top of their class, while the G70, G80, and G90 sedans are also strong offerings, bolstering Genesis' average score above its more well-established luxury competitors in our ratings.

Honda models regularly earn multiple spots on our annual list of 10Best award winners, so it's no surprise that this brand places highly here. The mainstream Accord, Civic, and CR-V comprise the core of the Honda lineup in terms of sales, but there's excellence to be found elsewhere, such as the Passport two-row SUV and the high-performance Si and Type R variants of the Civic.

Volkswagen may have shifted its focus towards SUVs in the U.S., but it still offers enthusiast favorites including the Golf GTI and Golf R that help bolster its reputation among car lovers. Plus, its SUV offerings are competitive, especially the Tiguan which places highly in our compact-SUV rankings.

BMW has a broad lineup ranging from small sedans to full-size, three-row SUVs. And there's a clear throughline within this portfolio, as most BMW models are competitive in their segments and offer the satisfying driving dynamics and refined powertrains we've come to expect from this German luxury marque.

Familiar Ford nameplates such as the Focus and Fusion have been gone for years now, as the Blue Oval now builds almost exclusively SUVs and trucks. But its SUVs and trucks are largely competitive, and there's plenty of fun to be had within the Bronco side of the corral. And of course, the Mustang pony car is still going strong.

Hyundai has an impressively full lineup of sedans, SUVs, and even a pickup truck, and it's taken the fight to stalwarts such as Honda and Toyota by offering many hybrid and battery-electric models in competitive segments. The Palisade Hybrid SUV and Ioniq 5 electric SUV are among the brand's current standout models.

Mazda earned its way into our hearts by building the MX-5 Miata sports car—and then by imbuing its more mainstream sedans and SUVs with the same fun-to-drive spirit. Some newer Mazdas have prioritized technology and size over driving enjoyment, so a few models have slipped in our ratings, but the brand still offers several models sitting at or near the top of their segments.

Despite being raised on a steady diet of base-model Hondas and Toyotas—or perhaps because of it—Joey Capparella cultivated an obsession for the automotive industry throughout his childhood in Nashville, Tennessee. He found a way to write about cars for the school newspaper during his college years at Rice University, which eventually led him to move to Ann Arbor, Michigan, for his first professional auto-writing gig at Automobile Magazine. He has been part of the Hearst Autos team since 2016 and now lives in New York City.

#4460. Repair Shop Quoted a Man $1,200 to Replace a $150 Muffler He Didn't Need

A “high-profile” repair shop quoted a man $1,264.40 to replace a muffler, when all he needed was a $17 exhaust gasket.

Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push

Car Loan Fraud Is Costing Billions As AI Makes Scams Harder To Spot

New Toyota RAV4 Has A Comfort Issue Some Owners Can't Ignore

Used EVs Are Selling Faster Than Gas Cars, but Tesla Isn't Leading

For a thousand bucks, you could get a lot of work done on your car, and a repair shop in Vermont reviewed a quote from a “high-profile” repair shop that could have cost a customer nearly ten times the cost of the part itself.

A video was posted on TikTok by mainly_mechanics (@mainly_mechanics) detailing a quote from another shop that appears to have overcharged a customer for a part that he didn’t even need.

It seems rather outrageous that a stock replacement muffler would cost over a thousand dollars to purchase. Apparently, it doesn’t cost that much, according to mainly_mechanics, while tagging TJ’s Auto Repair in Burlington, Vermont. In this video, he showed the quote that the other shop gave his customer.

The breakdown of the muffler replacement was as follows: $1,082 for the replacement muffler assembly, $17 for the gasket, and $4.24 for the nuts and bolts; then the rest is for about 48 minutes of labor, which totals $1,264.40. On the same quote was a note from the shop saying that the vehicle’s current muffler assembly “is rusted and leaks; will fail VSI (a.k.a. Vermont State Inspection).” The note is a bit of a scare tactic, which would otherwise render the car illegal to drive and register in Vermont.

The thing is, Vermont accepts repair jobs as long as the repair is as good as, or if not better than, OEM. A complete muffler replacement might not have been necessary in the first place if the muffler was damaged.

According to mainly_mechanics, the cost of a new muffler, if it were purchased by him as a business, would come out to $157 dollars. If the customer would like to purchase the part himself, the amount would go up by about ten bucks, and if the customer were to get the part through a retailer, it would total almost $300. Nowhere in any of mainly_mechanic’s quotes did they get even remotely close to $1,200, even after accounting for labor.

Including parts and labor, plus the $17 gasket, the $4.24 set of nuts and bolts, and the $159.99 for 48 minutes of labor, we get $348.23. That’s about a third of the price that the other shop would have charged the customer. The thing is, mainly_mechanics didn’t state this number themselves because, based on their assessment of the vehicle, the customer didn’t even need to buy a new muffler.

The main issue here isn’t just the price of the part, but the fact that the car didn’t even need it in the first place. Later in the video, mainly_mechanics then showed us the muffler that was supposed to be replaced. It was determined that the exhaust gasket and the bolts were the only things that needed replacing, as the leaks were coming from there.

Moving to the back of the car, there were no such leaks to speak of. There was some surface rust, but not enough that would punch a hole through the body of the muffler or any of the connecting pipes. If the customer went ahead and spent on just the gasket and the bolts, minus the labor, he would have come out about $21 bucks poorer, then maybe about a hundred bucks in labor for the simpler job, and the total might come out to around $150 more or less.

In defense of this “high-profile” shop, maybe the customer was given an initial diagnosis without a thorough underchassis inspection. Based on the available information on the post, it could have been an initial quote, which was there to give the customer an idea of just how expensive it could get. Now, if this shop actually conducted the inspection and then quoted the customer its price for the muffler replacement, then there’s a problem.

The car in question is also a mystery. There was no mention of a year, make, or model of the car, which doesn’t give us a clear picture of what prices to expect for replacement parts. With a list price of $284, though, according to mainly_mechanics, it also calls into question where the part is coming from, whether it’s from an OEM or aftermarket replacement manufacturer.

Mainly_mechanics didn’t go into detail about where he sourced the $157 replacement from. You could speculate that the part was an aftermarket OEM replacement, while the part that the “high-profile” shop was selling was from the manufacturer, which could explain the high cost, somewhat (not really). Aftermarket or third-party replacement parts are designed to deliver similar performance to the OEM part that they replace, though there is a difference in price and quality, which is noted by the Federal Trade Commission.

Still, a $900-plus profit does sound criminal, but a quote is not a charge. I’d make an issue if that “high-profile” shop ended up charging the customer, but it’s a good thing he managed to shop around before bringing out his wallet. I guess the lesson here is to be aware of your vehicle’s issue and make sure that the shop handling it does its due diligence by properly inspecting your vehicle and showing you what’s wrong with it before any quote is given.

Used electric vehicle prices have reversed course, climbing nearly 10% as budget-conscious buyers flock to the secondary market for affordable options.

Used EVs Are Selling Faster Than Gas Cars, but Tesla Isn't Leadingм

Toyota Tundra Owner Dodges $25,000 Repair His Truck Didn't Actually Need

Winter Weather Advisory Issued for Up to 15 Inches of Snow and 55 MPH Gusts Today

Rare Green Ferrari Daytona SP3 Sells for $18.5 Million

For the past two years, the narrative surrounding electric vehicles has been dominated by massive depreciation and sluggish showroom traffic. However, a significant shift is currently underway in the secondary market. As budget-conscious consumers actively seek out affordable alternatives to internal combustion, the demand for pre-owned electric models is suddenly accelerating at an unprecedented pace across the country.

This secondary market boom presents a stark contrast to the new vehicle sector. While expensive brand-new models continue facing long dealership dwell times, the pre-owned electric segment is currently setting records with buyers. Furthermore, as fluctuating fuel costs continue to heavily influence consumer buying habits, this sudden shift in buyer behavior is helping automakers see their EV sales jump when they focus on affordability and value.

According to a recent study by iSeeCars, used EV prices have surprisingly reversed their long downward trajectory, rising by approximately 9.8% overall. The broad takeaway from the report indicates that consumer demand is finally catching up with the available inventory. Buyers who were previously priced out of the electric transition are now enthusiastically scooping up heavily depreciated lease returns.

We have earlier reported that a massive flood of cheap electric vehicles would heavily disrupt residual values and cost manufacturers billions. However, this rising price trend proves that eager buyers are actively stepping in to absorb that inventory. In fact, deliberately adding more affordable used cars to the secondary market can ultimately benefit car companies in the long run by cultivating early brand loyalty. For those consumers who have been patiently waiting for the market to surge, the window to grab absolute rock-bottom pricing might be slowly closing as values naturally stabilize.

The timing of this price stabilization is incredibly critical for the broader automotive ecosystem. Throughout the year, roughly 300,000 used EVs hit dealership lots as early adopter lease programs expire, with more to come in the next few months. If prices had continued their brutal downward spiral, it would have created a catastrophic financial crisis for automotive finance arms and dealership networks alike.

Despite this almost 10% upward swing in used valuations, savvy consumers can still negotiate incredible bargains if they know where to look. By taking advantage of existing tax credits and heavily subsidized dealership promotions, shoppers can easily find the best EV deals available before the secondary market fully rebounds. This price correction proves that electric vehicles are finally establishing a healthy, sustainable lifecycle in the used car sector.

The Audacious Automotive IV is built on the B7 RS4 and has a claimed top speed of 200 mph.

Few cars have as famed a history as the Audi Quattro, and even fewer cars have been reimagined as many times. The newest tribute to Audi’s legendary Quattro is the Audacious Automotive IV. It’s being built by a small British manufacturer whose passion drove it to fit its creation with a V-8 that revs to 10,000 rpm.

The IV combines B7-generation Audi RS4 underpinnings with the look—and in some cases, bodywork—of the short-wheelbase Audi Quattro. While the Quattro was famous for its five-cylinder engine, Audacious felt the RS4’s 4.2-liter V-8 was a better fit for its tribute car.

See all results for used cars for sale near 33486

Coincidentally enough, the builder says the IV will be offered with four engine configurations. The standard setup takes the 4.2-liter V-8 and adds a supercharger, increasing power to 592 ponies. Strengthened internals and improved cooling from Audacious’ Stage Two conversion bring that figure to 740 hp. Plus, there are supercharged and naturally aspirated options that raise the engine’s redline from an already lofty 8250 to an otherworldly 10,000 rpm. It doesn’t seem like the higher redline offers any additional power, but it should sound the business.

Whichever engine customers choose, every IV will use the RS4’s original six-speed manual gearbox. Audacious claims the Quattro recreation will accelerate from zero to 60 mph in 3.4 seconds and reach a top speed of 200 mph, though the brand doesn’t disclose which configuration will reach that terminal velocity.

Customers can order their IV with metal bodywork sourced from an original Quattro donor, or they can have their car built from a new carbon-fiber body that doesn’t require any donor car. According to a report from Autocar, the company expects the latter to make up around 80 percent of its orders. The automaker is targeting a curb weight of around 2755 pounds for the carbon versions and around 3140 pounds for the donor cars.

Like the original Quattro, the interior has been overhauled to be a bit more raw, though at least in the examples shown, the whole thing is draped in leather. With every car being hand-built, Audacious promises that no two IVs will be exactly the same.

Of course, as a coachbuilt model produced by a team the size of Audacious Automotive, production will be extremely limited. It doesn’t hurt that exclusivity sells, and with the IV being limited to just 50 hand-built units worldwide, that number shouldn’t be too hard to hit. There is the price to consider, though, and the IV doesn’t come cheap, with a starting price of roughly $468,650 (based on current exchange rates).

#4455. Tesla drops car referral rewards, now pays owners in FSD for referrals

Tesla has launched a new referral program in the US that pays owners in Full Self-Driving (Supervised) instead of rewarding car sales. A referred owner gets one free month of FSD, and the referrer gets a free month or a $99 Tesla Credit if that person starts paying.

At the same time, Tesla’s Refer and Earn terms no longer list any vehicle as a qualifying purchase for buyer or referrer rewards. Buy a Tesla with a friend’s code today and neither of you gets anything.

To share a link, you need to be paying for FSD (Supervised) monthly or own it outright from before Tesla stopped selling it, according to Tesla’s FSD referral support page. Owners who got FSD through a one-year grant can’t participate. The link lives under “Refer and Earn” in the Tesla app, version 4.62.0 or later.

The person on the other end has to own a registered Tesla with compatible hardware, can’t have paid for FSD in the past 12 months, and can’t have bought it outright. There’s also a catch for recent buyers: anyone who got a free FSD trial with a new car is locked out of referral links until 12 months after that trial ends.

The bigger change is buried in Tesla’s Refer and Earn page. Buyer benefits now apply to solar panels only. Referrer benefits cover solar, first demo drives (up to 30 over an account’s lifetime) and the new FSD referral.

Model 3, Model Y and Cybertruck only show up under loyalty benefits, for existing owners buying another Tesla product. Model S and Model X aren’t listed at all.

Tesla didn’t announce the change. The page is stamped “Updated February 24, 2026,” so it’s unclear exactly when vehicles came off the list.

That’s quite a turn for a program that was always about moving cars. When Tesla brought the referral program back in August 2024, a buyer got $1,000 off a Model S, X, Y or 3, and the referrer got $500 in credit. Tesla has killed and revived the program several times over the past decade, but cars were always at the center of it. Not anymore.

That’s the exact metric in Elon Musk’s 2025 CEO Performance Award, which includes a milestone of 10 million active FSD subscriptions. It’s the reason Tesla started disclosing the number in January in the first place.

The free month a friend receives doesn’t count toward that total. A paid conversion does, and that’s precisely the event the new program pays for.

The only way I would ever pay for FSD is if Tesla covered full comprehensive insurance for my vehicle and accepted all liability. Otherwise, it's a gamble with my (and others') life.

That they seem to prioritize this sham service (Just call it Assisted Driving for honesty sake?) versus improving the cars or lowering prices, tells me enough not to look at Tesla for my next vehicle.

The recipient has to already own a Tesla, so the program doesn’t add a single car to the fleet. It’s built to mine the existing fleet for subscriptions. Tesla had sold about 8.9 million vehicles by the end of 2025, and only 1.74 million are paying for FSD, so there’s plenty of room. At Q3’s pace, we estimated 10 million subscriptions is still about eight years away.

So Tesla stopped paying for referrals that require selling a car, and started paying for the ones that move the number in Musk’s pay package. We think that tells you a lot about where the company’s priorities are right now.

#4454. Diablo 4's next expansion is bringing two new classes to the game, one of which you can play right now

Lord of Hatred may finally make good on the Mephisto arc of Diablo 4's campaign, which started in the original game and carried through Vessel of Hatred.

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a big deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the new War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

#4453. Corvette SUV and Electric Sports Car Plans Reportedly Shelved

Just 11% of Gas-Car Owners See an EV as Their Likely Next Buy

BMW Employs Professional Sniffers to Eliminate New Car Smell

Bugatti CEO Chased His Stolen Chiron Across Borders in a Porsche 911

They were reportedly expected to launch by 2026, but so far, there’s been nothing but crickets.

Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push

Car Loan Fraud Is Costing Billions As AI Makes Scams Harder To Spot

New Toyota RAV4 Has A Comfort Issue Some Owners Can't Ignore

Used EVs Are Selling Faster Than Gas Cars, but Tesla Isn't Leading

The electric vehicle market had strong momentum at the start of this decade, with Ford even expanding the Mustang lineup with an EV spin-off called the Mustang Mach-E. Reports also suggest that Chevrolet once considered expanding the Corvette lineup with two new all-electric models, an SUV and a two-door sports car. But apparently, the automaker may have already shelved those plans.

According to GM Authority, plans for the SUV, internally codenamed V224, and the two-door EV, codenamed V284, have been put on hold. A fastback spin-off was also reportedly in the works, though the publication is less certain about its existence. These vehicles were initially expected to launch between 2025 and 2026, but with this year nearing its end, none have materialized so far.

The report also didn’t offer an explanation for why GM reportedly shelved the potential expansion. But given the slowing demand for EVs, especially in the U.S., these models could face less favorable market conditions. The Corvette SUV may be worth looking at, as this type of vehicle continues to see sustained demand. If the SUV version takes off, it could potentially generate revenue to support the Corvette lineup and further expansion plans. Lamborghini demonstrates this lineup dynamic with the Urus, which continues to be its best-selling model over its traditional supercar offerings. However, an all-electric powertrain could introduce additional uncertainties.

In fact, in the third quarter of this year, GM’s EV sales declined 62% compared to the same period last year. Sure, Q3 2025 saw a huge spike in sales as buyers rushed their EV purchases before the $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired, but slowing EV sales have also affected other brands. Ford even ended production of the all-electric F-150 Lightning, while Ram dropped plans for an all-electric 1500 in favor of a range-extended version.

What’s more interesting is that Corvette sales are up. The American sports car sold 6,585 units in Q3 2026, a 28.5% increase over the 5,123 units sold during the same period last year. This could tell the automaker that the current formula is working, and that now may not be the right time to commit resources to developing new models.

However, these reports have not been confirmed by GM itself. One of the automaker’s latest electrification developments involves preparing its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant for future hybrid production, which could help it capitalize on growing demand for hybrids in the U.S. The Corvette remains its sole hybrid offering with the Grand Sport X and the more extreme ZR1X, the latter capable of generating 1,250 horsepower.

To be fair, reports of the expansion plan date back to 2022, so jumping on the EV bandwagon may have been worth the risk at the time. Times are changing, and seeing the expansion plan reportedly shelved isn’t much of a surprise. However, Corvette chief engineer Tony Roma recently said that the nameplate will eventually go fully electric, but don’t expect it anytime soon.

#4452. How Well Would the New Dodge Charger Work on ‘The Dukes of Hazzard’?

Much of the discourse around the current Dodge Charger has concerned Dodge’s decisions to eliminate V-8 engines, use a shared body for two-doors and four-doors, and offer an electric version. I don’t care about any of that, because there’s another question that is much more central to the Charger’s very existence, and nobody’s talking about it enough. And that is: What would the Dukes of Hazzard think about the new Dodge Charger?Our search analytics indicate that this question gets asked hundreds of times every day, although that number does drop significantly when my computer battery is dead. Therefore, it must be answered, and I am a unique authority on this subject, having driven the 2026 Dodge Charger and watched The Dukes of Hazzard—yes, both the 1979–1985 TV series and the Johnny Knoxville 2005 feature film. In fact, in kindergarten I got sent inside at recess because I was “spinning my tires” (kicking dirt while making Dodge Charger engine noises) and a clump of soil flew into a classmate’s ice cream. Why did she have ice cream at recess and I didn’t? Why did she blithely stand so close to Bo Duke fleeing Sheriff Rosco P. Coltrane? Even worse, once I got sent inside, another kid in detention told the teacher that I’d been swearing when I hadn’t, and I got in even more trouble. Just good old boys, never meaning no harm? I can relate.

See all results for new 2026 Dodge Charger for sale near 42082

Hazzard County was filled with memorable characters. There were the titular Dukes, as well as Cooter the mechanic, Rosco the sheriff, and the nefarious Boss Hogg. But the main character, really, was a car: the General Lee, Bo and Luke Duke’s 1969 Dodge Charger. The General Lee had a huge Confederate flag on the roof, because that was how 1979 TV executives made sure you remembered the show was set in Georgia. There really weren’t many other clues, given that after the first five episodes, everything was shot in sunny, dry, brown California, and not many of the cast members even bothered trying to fake a Southern accent. Besides the Confederate flag livery, the General Lee was named the General Lee.

It was also supposed to be an ex–race car, so the doors were welded shut and Bo and Luke had to climb in through the windows. So our first question for the new Charger is whether it’s easy to climb through the window in a hurry, as one would when being chased by Rosco or even his dimwitted deputy, Enos.

Climbing in through the driver’s-side window of a 2026 Charger—in my test case, the four-door Scat Pack—is not easy, and I doubt it would be much different on the two-door, with its longer window. That’s because the Charger’s window aperture is a maximum of about 13 inches tall, and the sill is more than 41 inches off the Hazzard County dirt. Climbing in through the Charger window might require some pole-vaulting experience as you Fosbury flop into the driver’s seat. I bet it would be easier when fueled by the adrenaline of a chase, either fleeing from Rosco or in pursuit of a bad guy who’s come to town for the day.

See all results for new 2026 Dodge Charger for sale near 42082

The Charger’s largeness also impedes the other signature Dukes getting-in-the-car move, which is sliding across the hood on a run. The Dukes seldom had time to run around the car, let alone walk, so they’d slide across the hood as a helpful shortcut. The Charger’s hood is tall, like the windowsill, and the Scat Pack also has an inset textured Six Pack-logo fake vent toward the front of the hood, in the prime sliding area.

What was Dodge thinking, adding a source of friction that could end up being the difference between jail and making it across the Chickasaw County line? The electric Charger Daytona might be even worse, with its plunging hood and front wing. Try to slide across that, and you might get stuck in it, ending up utterly humiliated as Rosco stands there and excitedly says, “Goo, goo, goo!” That is what Rosco said when he was happy and excited. That and “Cuff ’em and stuff ’em!”

But we don’t think that Bo and Luke would have driven a Charger Daytona. Maybe Coy and Vance would have. They were the alternate guys who showed up when the actual Duke actors, Tom Wopat and John Schneider, held out at the start of Season 5 in a contract dispute. Before there was Temu, Coy and Vance were shorthand for a shoddy imitation, and fans hated them. Look, we can believe that you can accurately shoot a flaming arrow out the window of a car that’s in the middle of a 120-foot gap jump, but you’re telling us Bo and Luke left Hazzard to pursue NASCAR careers, just leaving Daisy and Uncle Jesse to the predations of Boss Hogg? As if. The suspension of disbelief only goes so far, and it was the most galling casting move until New Becky appeared on Roseanne.

Once Bo and Luke made it into the 2026 Charger and got moving, the first thing they’d notice is the power. Well, the first thing they’d probably notice is the seatbelt chime because they weren’t real sticklers for safety. But then they’d appreciate the Scat Pack’s 550 horsepower and its all-wheel drive. The General Lee was constantly struggling for traction on Hazzard’s roads, both paved and unpaved alike, but the 2026 model digs in and goes—witness the two-door’s 3.7-second blast to 60 mph. However, when the mood suits, you can disable the front axle for drifting, like when you need to slide the car around in a tight pivot to hide behind a roadside billboard. And the six is paired with an eight-speed automatic, which means that on a curvy road you’ll hear lots of upshifts and downshifts, just like the General Lee. The 1969 Charger had a three-speed automatic, but in Hazzard you could sometimes hear it upshift about 10 times. Probably something to do with the acoustics of the hollers.What else? Well, the 2026 Charger’s hatchback body means it has plenty of room for hauling moonshine. It is built by the same company that owns Jeep, so Daisy would still drive one of those. The horn goes “honk” but does not play a melody from the song “Dixie.” There is no orange paint option, or should I say, there’s no orange paint option yet. Is there anything else that people identify with the Dukes and their car? I can’t think of any that I might compare.

Oh, wait. There is one thing. It would involve a, uh, suspension test. And here I will shamefully admit that I cannot authoritatively say whether the 2026 Charger can handle a jump of more than 200 feet, because the loan agreements we sign to test cars generally forbid that sort of thing. I’m making my way, the only way I know how. But that’s just a little bit more than the law will allow.

Ezra Dyer is a Car and Driver senior editor and columnist. He's now based in North Carolina but still remembers how to turn right. He owns a 2009 GEM e4 and once drove 206 mph. Those facts are mutually exclusive.

#4451. The highly-anticipated follow-up to Baldur's Gate 3 is more Divinity, but it's not technically Original Sin 3

Larian has returned to tease a grand vision for its next major project, a new Divinity.

Larian Studios has delivered what was arguably the biggest reveal of The Game Awards 2025 showcase. The Hellstone, the mysterious monolith in the desert that’s been generating a lot of speculation in the lead-up to the show was indeed teasing the studio’s next game.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next big thing in the space.

Larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” said founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

“This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”

Beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. We do know it’s an RPG, so you can very much expect something similar to earlier games in the series, and, of course, Baldur’s Gate 3.

The differences between automotive markets are interesting; some regions require certain cars in segments that don’t sell well elsewhere. In other cases, brands repurpose and revive nameplates they no longer use to enter a segment they want to compete in.

That’s the case for one of Toyota’s most recognized models that had a long run but was recently killed off. The Avalon used to be a staple in Toyota’s lineup, but made way for the Crown’s entry in the U.S.; however, in China, the Avalon lives on and is getting a new model too.

Autohome reports it learned from official brand sources that the new Toyota Avalon for China will launch on November 5. The new Avalon will feature exterior and interior upgrades and offer both gasoline and hybrid variants.

On the outside, the first major change is the redesigned front grille, now featuring vertical chrome slats as the main design element. Above that grille is the now-iconic Toyota C-shaped headlight cluster we see on the Crown and the Camry, to which the Avalon is closely related. Size-wise, the new Avalon measures 4,990 mm (length), 1,850 mm (width), and 1,440 mm (height), with a wheelbase of 2,870 mm. The rims now feature a new design, while the rear lighting cluster sets the Avalon apart from its Toyota sedan siblings with its own distinct pattern and layout.

The Avalon was always supposed to be an elevated Camry, bridging the gap between that model and the higher Lexus cars. That’s evident in the new Avalon’s interior, which features a wraparound design with a large infotainment screen, a HUD, and crystal trim that contrasts with the subtle two-tone piping on the seats and steering wheel. It also has other notable features like heated and ventilated seats, massaging functions for the front passengers, and an in-car fragrance system.

In terms of the powertrain, the Avalon will be offered with either a 2.0-liter gasoline engine that makes 170 hp, which is the same as the current Avalon, or a 2.5-liter gasoline-hybrid system that makes a combined 230 hp. The 2.0-liter gets a normal CVT, while the hybrid gets a specialized e-CVT.

#4448. BYD reveals a flashy new feature on its upcoming luxury EV

BYD is moving upmarket with its new flagship EV, featuring suicide doors, a gemstone grille, and possibly solid-state batteries.

Yangwang is like BMW’s Rolls-Royce and Mercedes-Maybach, sitting at the very top of BYD’s brand hierarchy.

The ultra-luxury brand offers BYD’s most high-end and technically advanced vehicles, including the U7 sedan, the U8, a hardcore off-road SUV, and the U9, an electric supercar.

Yangwang vehicles have previously debuted with BYD’s latest breakthrough tech, including its quad-motor e4 platform (delivering over 1,300 hp), its second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging, and its DiSus-X intelligent body control system.

Its next model will push further into the elite segment. After BYD revealed the name of its new flagship executive sedan earlier this week, the Yangwang Altior, the company has released several new details ahead of its official debut.

Yangwang general manager Hu Xiaoqing confirmed on Friday that the new Yangwang Altior will feature suicide doors, a first for a BYD model.

The new door design swings open nearly 90 degrees, Hu said, creating a dramatic, wide-open entrance.

Hu also posted a preview of the vehicle’s front fascia, complete with a dot-matrix Gemstrone grille and crystal-inspired headlights.

BYD has not confirmed many details, but the ultra-luxury sedan is expected to be about 5,500 mm (216″) in length.

Images of the disguised vehicle released last month show a similar shape and size to the Mercedes-Benz Maybach S-Class or Rolls-Royce Phantom.

HU said last week that the global launch of the new flagship sedan will take place in the UAE, not in BYD’s home market of China.

BYD has not revealed an official date, but according to CarNewsChina, citing “sources familiar with the project,” BYD aims to unveil the new flagship model in Dubai, UAE, around November 5.

The Yangwang Altrio will feature “unprecedented disruptive technology,” Zheng Yu, Yangwang’s executive general manager, said.

In one image, the vehicle was charging at a BYD Flash Charge station, suggesting it will use its Blade Battery 2.0 and 5-minute Flash Charging technology.

There are companies showcasing flying cars designed specifically for circus-style shows, while others are launching solid-state batteries that can recharge in five minutes.

I find myself wondering—though perhaps not too deeply—which of these technologies will secure the largest customer base and generate the greatest returns for shareholders.

Outside of the suicide doors, rumors suggest the flagship model will be BYD’s first vehicle to use solid-state batteries. Executive vice president Stella Li said during an interview with Carwow.es last month that BYD’s first vehicle to use solid-state batteries will debut in 2027.

The executive sedan is expected to debut around November 5. Prices are rumored to start in the 2 million yuan range, or about $300,000.

When it comes to lighting innovations, Audi has many accomplishments, especially with LEDs. For instance, the D3 (second-gen) Audi A8 was the very first car to feature LED daytime running lights. After that, it was the first-generation R8 that became that had full LED illumination, front and rear.

Then, the third-generation A8 became the first production car with matrix LED lighting, after that, the TT RS became one of the first cars to have OLED tail lights. In other words, Audi has done a lot for the world of vehicle lighting, and many of its innovations have become commonplace today.

It seems that the folks from Ingolstadt want to keep its lighting innovations streak going by introducing yet another world-first. Its latest bit of lighting tech can be seen in the Q9, and it’s the very first one in the world to be available with curved OLED exterior lighting. While that doesn’t sound all too exciting, this has all the potential to change how rear lights are lit and designed.

One could say that this has allowed Audi to bend light, figuratively speaking, of course. By curving the OLED panel, it lets brake lights and turn signals be more visible from the corners of the vehicle. But the main advantage of doing this is surface uniformity, and OLEDs deliver uniform illumination without the need for point bulbs or reflectors.

The carrier glass of these OLEDs measures just 0.1 millimeters thick, which is 1/256ths of an inch. For easier visualization, that’s roughly the thickness of a hair strand, and that’s allowed Audi to ‘bend’ the panel to a significant degree. That allows the panel to follow the contours of the vehicle, as well as giving designers more freedom to explore more daring light designs.

As Audi has been making OLEDs for a decade now, it’s learned enough to move the technology forwards. Now in it’s the third-iteration, the Q9 boasts the has the largest OLED panel Audi has built to date. It has a total of 512 segments spread across six digital OLED panels. The individually controllable segments give the Q9’s rear lights multiple static, active, or semi-active digital light signatures, as well as project warning symbols.

It’s worth pointing out that these curved OLEDs are not fitted to all Q9 trims. If you want these lights, you can only get these in the Prestige model, as it’s not optional on both base Premium and mid-spec Premium Plus variants. These lights are fitted as standard in the SQ9.

#4446. Arc Raiders' Cold Snap update brings snow storms to most maps, new events and a new Raider Deck

Arc Raiders has delivered a big new update that's very fittingly on theme, and it's not without new mechanics.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive update. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and new frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

One of the new events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

While on the subject, the new update also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

#4444. Honda has dominated motorcycles for decades. Electric bikes are changing that

Honda has spent decades building one of the most dominant positions in the global motorcycle industry, selling millions of gasoline-powered two-wheelers each year. But in markets where electric motorcycles and scooters are becoming increasingly accessible, that dominance is starting to face a serious challenge.

Vietnam offers a particularly interesting case study, where rapidly growing electric motorcycle sales are beginning to reshape a market long dominated by Honda.

According to newly released nationwide sales figures, Vietnam saw more than 3 million motorcycle and scooter sales during the first nine months of 2026, representing 25.9% growth over the same period last year.

But the real story is in the electric segment, where sales surged 90.5% to reach 973,247 units. That means electric two-wheelers now account for approximately 32% of all new motorcycle and scooter sales in the country.

And the biggest beneficiary isn’t Honda. It’s actually Vietnamese electric vehicle manufacturer VinFast.

While Honda remains Vietnam’s largest motorcycle manufacturer overall, with sales growing 8.4% this year, VinFast has surged into second place with a staggering 152.1% increase in sales. Yamaha now sits in third place, followed by electric two-wheeler manufacturer Yadea in fourth.

Of the top four players, half are electric, and it’s precisely that half that is experiencing meteoric sales growth.

It’s an impressive reshuffling of a market that has traditionally been dominated by Japanese gasoline motorcycle manufacturers.

Vietnam’s transition hasn’t happened in a vacuum, either. Government efforts to reduce urban air pollution, including plans to restrict gasoline-powered motorcycles in parts of Hanoi, have helped create an increasingly favorable environment for electric alternatives.

Too bad for Honda but I'm thrilled to read about increasing sales of electric motorcycles. I don't live in or near Vietnam but the pollution from small gasoline engines affects everyone where the wind blows it.

And with companies like VinFast offering an expanding range of electric scooters and motorcycles, riders now have more practical alternatives to gasoline-powered models than ever before.

To be clear, Honda isn’t exactly struggling. Its motorcycle sales are still growing, and the Japanese giant remains the undisputed market leader in Vietnam. But its overall share of the market is shrinking, and its relatively modest growth compared to the exploding electric segment suggests that the market’s center of gravity is beginning to shift.

Vietnam may be just a single example, but it’s an important one of what can happen when electric two-wheelers become viable mainstream alternatives to gasoline motorcycles.

Honda has spent decades perfecting the gasoline motorcycle. The question now is how quickly it can adapt to a market that is increasingly interested in something else.
