#4417. Electric trucks hit 50% of China’s heavy truck sales, diesel demand falls

Electric trucks made up 50.3% of all heavy trucks sold in China in September. That’s 33,100 electric big rigs in a single month, up 37% from a year ago, while the overall heavy-truck market shrank by 21%.

And it’s showing up in the oil data. China’s diesel demand is on track to fall by about 230,000 barrels per day this year, and trucks running on batteries and natural gas are doing most of the work.

In 2024, new-energy vehicles accounted for 13.6% of heavy trucks (12 tonnes and up) sold in China. In 2025, sales nearly tripled to 231,100 units, up 182%, for a 28.9% share.

December 2025 hit 53.9%, but that was a rush. Buyers piled in before trade-in subsidies expired and new purchase tax costs kicked in, and the share dropped back to about 23% by March.

Then it came right back. Through the first nine months of 2026, China sold 226,400 electric heavy trucks, up 64%, for a 38.1% share. That’s already almost as many as in all of 2025, with a quarter still to go. In tractors, the big rigs that pull long-haul trailers, the September share hit 64.5%.

That’s well ahead of Beijing’s own plan. This year, 11 government bodies set a target of 40% new-energy heavy-truck sales by 2030, along with 1.6 million of them on the road, 30,000 km of zero-carbon freight corridors and about 3,000 charging and swap stations. The market blew past that sales target four years early on a monthly basis, and CATL now says new-energy trucks will be half of China’s annual truck sales by 2028.

It comes down to cost. In most uses, an electric heavy truck in China is now cheaper to own and run than a diesel one, and fleets run that math every day.

CATL claims savings of about 0.6 yuan per km. Independent numbers are more measured, but still favorable: a study by the ICCT and China’s CATARC found battery-electric trucks about 19% cheaper per tonne-km than diesel in good conditions, though they lose that edge at low annual mileage or when battery weight eats into payload.

Charging time is the other objection, and China’s answer is swapping. CATL’s Qiji brand operated about 300 heavy-truck swap stations at the end of 2025 and plans 900 by the end of this year and 2,000 in 2027. In August, it agreed to pay 2.56 billion yuan (about $370 million) for nearly 25% of Qiyuan Green Power, China’s largest heavy-truck swap operator with more than 1,600 charging and swap stations. Its new standardized packs hold 432 kWh and 513 kWh and swap in about five minutes.

CATL is already taking the swapping model to Europe with Octopus Energy.

The trucks themselves are domestic. XCMG led the segment in 2025 with a 15.4% share, ahead of SANY and FAW Jiefang, and the top three held 42.9% of the market. CATL supplied 60% of the batteries.

For years, the alternative to diesel trucks in China was liquefied natural gas. LNG trucks took nearly 30% of the market in 2024, when gas was much cheaper than diesel.

Now they’re losing to batteries. According to Kpler, LNG trucks had a 37% share of heavy-duty registrations in March, against 23% for electric. By July, electric was at 47% and LNG had collapsed to 11%. Monthly LNG truck registrations fell from more than 30,000 to about 6,200.

So China is skipping the “bridge fuel” phase for trucks almost as fast as it started it.

China’s diesel consumption already peaked. Rhodium Group found that diesel refinery runs topped out in April 2023, and apparent consumption dropped from 4.7 million barrels per day then to 4.0 million barrels per day in April 2025.

2026 is the steepest drop yet. Kpler estimates diesel demand fell about 420,000 barrels per day year-over-year in May, roughly 10%, and 460,000 in June. It expects a decline of about 230,000 barrels per day for the full year and only a 64,000 barrel-per-day rebound in 2027.

Kpler puts the gross diesel displacement from alternative trucks at about 680,000 barrels per day this year: roughly 450,000 from the LNG fleet built in recent years and 230,000 from electric trucks. Road freight still grew about 3% through July. China is moving more goods with less diesel.

There’s a catch. The fuel price spike this spring, tied to the Iran war, cut demand on its own and pushed more fleets toward electric. But that only explains part of it, and the fleet is still early: electric trucks will be only about 8% of China’s heavy trucks on the road by the end of 2026, according to Kpler. Every year of 40-50% sales shares compounds the diesel losses.

Europe is growing fast from a tiny base. ACEA data shows 5,120 heavy electric trucks (16 tonnes and up) registered in the EU through September, up 59.9%, for a 2.5% share. That’s up from 1.7% a year ago, but diesel still took 91.7% of all EU truck registrations.

A few countries stand out. Switzerland is at 24%, Norway 14.4%, the Netherlands 11.1% and Sweden 10.3%. Germany registered the most units at 1,722, but that’s only a 4.2% share.

The US doesn’t publish an official electric Class 8 sales figure, and that tells you something. The best indicator is the recent order for 2,500 Tesla Semis through ZET SCALE, which would roughly double the number of electric Class 8 trucks on US roads. Against about 230,000 Class 8 trucks sold per year, the electric share is well under 1%.

Price is the big difference. The ICCT puts the median electric Class 8 tractor in the US at $411,200, against $172,500 for diesel. Federal tax credits for commercial EVs ended in 2025, and California shelved the rule that would have required fleets to buy zero-emission trucks.

This is the biggest under-covered story in the EV industry right now.

Everyone argued for years about whether electric semis could work. Range, weight, charging, cost. China settled it the boring way. It got the price of a battery-electric heavy truck close enough to diesel, built swap stations along freight routes, and let fleet operators do what fleet operators always do: pick the cheapest truck per kilometer.

And the result is showing up where it matters, in oil demand. Trucks are where diesel lives. Displacing a quarter of a million barrels a day in one year, with electric trucks still only around 8% of the fleet, means we’re still early on this curve.

The contrast with the US is hard to watch. America has Tesla, a Semi factory in Nevada built for 50,000 trucks a year, and some of the best freight corridors in the world for electrification. But electric Class 8 trucks cost 2.4 times as much as diesel here, the federal incentives are gone, and the market is under 1%. The ZET SCALE order is real progress. But it came from shippers pooling their demand, and twe have yet to see these trucks get delivered.

China having a lot of phev and EV vehicles has helped with oil pricing around the world, more notably in the current american-caused oil crisis. It would be worse if they were all traditional powered cars and trucks.

Now to be clear, I'm not saying that it has made a massive impact or is even the only reason why the oil crisis isn't much worse, it's just one of a few steps China made to reduce the impact of the oil crisis. But going electric everywhere we can has a stabilizing effect when oil shocks show up

Europe at least has the regulation, and its best markets, at 10% to 24%, are roughly where China was in 2024 and 2025.

The question now is how long Chinese truck makers stay home. SANY and BYD already sell electric trucks in Europe, and CATL is building the swap network for them. If those trucks can come close to China’s pricing, how long can Western truck makers keep charging 2x diesel?

Diesel trucks aren’t the only thing batteries are displacing. At home, pairing solar with an EV or a home battery can cut your energy bills dramatically. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. #4415. Lexus is taking a page from China for its next electric SUV launching in 2027

Toyota’s luxury brand Lexus is launching a new electric SUV in 2027, its first vehicle built in China in over two decades.

It’s official. Toyota is breaking from tradition, planning to develop and produce the new vehicle in China rather than its home market of Japan.

Lexus confirmed the new vehicle will be made at its new manufacturing plant in Jinshan, Shanghai, and will go on sale in 2027.

As the first Lexus factory built from scratch overseas, the company said the new plant will bring together its global manufacturing capabilities.

Toyota broke ground on the facility in June 2025, saying the new facility will unlock “Lexus speed” as it aims to keep pace with domestic brands like BYD. Construction was expected to be completed this past August, with the first vehicle scheduled to roll off the assembly line in the fall of 2027.

The first Lexus model will be an electric SUV, produced using advanced manufacturing methods such as gigacasting to reduce costs and speed up output.

The facility will be a cornerstone of Toyota’s comeback plans in China, where it’s struggled to compete with local brands.

Production capacity will be around 1,000 units per month in 2027 as Toyota ramps up to “tens of thousands” in 2028.

Toyota’s sales plunged nearly 20% in China last month, marking its eighth consecutive month with lower sales than the year prior. The market in China “remained weak due in part to rising gasoline prices, while the market for gasoline vehicles and hybrid vehicles was particularly affected,” Toyota said.

In the first nine months of 2026, Toyota sold just over 1.05 million vehicles in China, 18.9% fewer than in the same period last year.

Lexus’ new Shanghai facility is wholly owned by Toyota, enabling it to produce vehicles in China through its joint ventures.

The new electric SUV will go on sale in China in 2027. Specific details, including battery, range, and prices, have yet to be announced.

As part of its “with China, for China, strategy, Lexus said it will “continue to use China as a source of innovation,” adding it will “deepen localization efforts” to bring classic models to the market that meet local needs.

Toyota joins the growing list of major OEMs that are already tapping, or plan to tap, China for its next-generation electric vehicles.

While in other global markets, Toyota is sticking to its “multi-pathway” strategy, which includes all powertrains from electric to ICE; in China, it’s being forced to adapt.

China is Toyota’s third-largest market, following the US and Japan. To stay competitive and turn things around in China, Toyota will rely more on local partners and suppliers.

Developing the new Lexus electric SUV in China first rather than Japan is significant given Toyota’s traditional ways.

Typically, it takes Toyota about four to five years to fully develop a new vehicle. In China, automakers are now building them in as little as two years.

Toyota, like many automakers at this point, is turning to China for new tech, batteries, production methods, and other EV components to keep pace.

You don’t always need an overtly sporty car to enjoy great driving dynamics. Even regular cars can be fun behind the wheel, bringing some joy to one’s everyday commute. Some shining examples include the Mazda3 and Honda Civic, while moving up the price bracket, you have compact executive sedans like the Alfa Romeo Giulia and BMW 3 Series.

Still, the list isn’t long enough, reckons Kia, as its chief ride and handling engineer for Australia, Graeme Gambold, said driving enthusiasts are being overlooked. He also mentioned that technology, while good, has been taking away the fun element in cars.

Speaking to Australian motoring publication Carsales, Gambold expressed his frustration towards some driver assist technologies. “It’s really hard to find a car that drives nicely. It’s really hard to find a car that has all the features but none of the safety intervention, as I don’t need it,” said the engineer.

Now, that’s a pretty bold statement from a company chief, especially since automakers are committed to advanced driver assist technologies. He’s not saying that those should be banned altogether, as there have been instances wherein these were genuine lifesavers. Instead, it’s the intrusiveness of these systems that annoys instead of giving joy.

Carsales also asked Gambold if fun cars are a dying art. While he said it wasn’t necessarily the case, he stated that current market priorities have put enthusiasts aside. It’s one of the reasons why Kia (along with Hyundai) still has ride and handling tuning divisions in its major markets. In an age where everyone is trying to shave chunks of cost, the South Korean automaker is more than willing to spend on catering its chassis to specific markets.

Right now, the main priority seems to be pushing out new models at lightning speed. It’s something that the Chinese market has effectively pressured legacy automakers to do, particularly in the fields of technology and electrification. But while higher-end models come with tricky suspension arrangements, one has to wonder how these cars would actually fare without these. It’s possible that electronics could be masking what are, otherwise, shortcomings in basic chassis tuning.

That’s the rub of the more widespread availability of active and adaptive suspension systems. While it’s good that the trickle-down effect has made these reasonably-priced options, it does make chassis engineering more tech-dependent, which also adds a layer of complexity to any vehicle. As China has effectively pressured the world into developing cars faster, and a majority of car buyers simply want point A to B transport, it doesn’t really encourage automakers to add a little zing to their mass-market models.

Of course, there may come a time when cars can be completely software-defined. Many automakers aren’t exactly shy about going in that direction. Still, at least we know some brands still see value in proper chassis tuning and calibration rather than just letting active systems and software development do a good chunk of the work.

#4413. BYD sold more EVs last month than the US did all quarter, topping 300,000

BYD sold over 300,000 electric vehicles in October, a new record and more than the US managed in the entire third quarter.

The world’s leading EV maker is showing no signs of slowing down. BYD sold 490,168 new energy vehicles (NEVs) in October, up 11% from the prior year and the company’s highest monthly total in 2026.

BYD’s battery electric vehicles drove the growth, with a record 305,743 units sold, up 37% year over year and marking the first time its EV sales have crossed the 300,000 mark.

To put that into perspective, just over 262,500 EVs were sold in the US in the entire third quarter combined, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates.

October marked BYD’s sixth straight month of higher sales growth and its third straight month of higher EV sales. Through October, BYD sold 1,953,700 electric vehicles, up 6% from the same period last year.

BYD’s all-electric vehicles (EVs) accounted for about 63% of total sales last month. Plug-in hybrid vehicles, meanwhile, fell 17% in October to 177,382 units. Through October, BYD’s PHEV sales fell 11% to 1,625,969 units.

According to BYD’s filing, the company exported 170,194 vehicles in October as it expands overseas to drive growth in markets like Europe, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America.

Through October, BYD exported over 1.5 million electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, nearly double compared to last year.

By the end of 2026, BYD expects overseas shipments to reach about 2 million vehicles. In 2027, that number is expected to rise to more than 2.5 million vehicles.

With several new and updated vehicles launching with its new Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology, BYD aims to continue attracting new buyers with longer range, faster charging, and more tech-oriented models.

While the US is coming off its best quarter of the year in EV sales, BYD’s performance shows how far ahead China is in the transition to electric vehicles.

China continues to lead the global EV market, accounting for over half of all electric cars sold worldwide.

With a wave of low-cost domestic brands flooding China’s market, BYD and other automakers are driving growth overseas in major markets like Europe, South Korea, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America, where legacy OEMs are already falling behind quickly.

A 1997 Ferrari F50 showing just 106 original miles recently sold for $17 million. This transaction establishes a new public pricing record for the 1990s Italian supercar, reflecting a sustained secondary market demand for ultra-low mileage collector vehicles. As automotive investors increasingly target analog supercars from this specific era, the financial benchmark for pristine Maranello halo cars continues to shift upward.

This specific chassis is the exact vehicle we reported earlier when it first became available to the public. While initial industry estimates boldly suggested the supercar might surpass the $20 million mark, the $17 million closing price still comfortably exceeds all previous public sales figures. It secures the vehicle’s position as one of the most valuable modern Ferraris in existence, bridging the historical gap between the turbocharged F40 and the technologically advanced Enzo.

According to a recent post on the Hagerty Instagram page, this chassis stands as one of the lowest-mileage F50s in existence. The vehicle spent the last two decades secured in a climate-controlled collection, effectively preserving its factory-delivered condition and maximizing its appeal to high-end buyers. In the elite collector car market, an unblemished, 106-mile odometer reading from 1997 transforms a vehicle from a mere sports car into a heavily scrutinized blue-chip asset.

F50 valuations have climbed steadily over the last decade as collectors recognize the rarity of the analog driving experience. While earlier examples sold for significantly less, even when carrying notable celebrity ownership, current market dynamics have fundamentally changed. Today’s serious automotive investors place a substantially higher financial premium on absolute delivery-mileage preservation and mechanical originality rather than focusing on a vehicle’s specific ownership history or famous previous drivers.

Ferrari originally engineered the F50 to celebrate the company’s 50th anniversary, purposefully utilizing a naturally aspirated 4.7-liter V12 engine derived directly from its 1990 Formula 1 racing program. Pushing 512 horsepower through a traditional six-speed manual transmission, the carbon-fiber chassis famously lacked power steering, power brakes, and modern stability control. Because the automaker strictly capped total global production at just 349 units, any surviving F50 remains an exceptionally rare acquisition on the open market.

To command top market value at this elite financial level, a collector-grade F50 must include absolutely all of its original accessories. This specific sale meticulously included the factory flight cases, the removable hardtop with its dedicated stand, the soft top, and the matching customized luggage. Maintaining these rare factory gems is strictly required to fully authenticate a vehicle’s provenance, pass intensive judging standards, and successfully achieve a record-setting final sale price of this magnitude.

#4410. Porsche Is Exploring a Way to Silence the Engine Drone in EVs

Just 11% of Gas-Car Owners See an EV as Their Likely Next Buy

BMW Employs Professional Sniffers to Eliminate New Car Smell

Bugatti CEO Chased His Stolen Chiron Across Borders in a Porsche 911

Porsche is poking around for ways to hush up range-extended EVs, and they’re not just stuffing more insulation under the carpet.

Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push

Car Loan Fraud Is Costing Billions As AI Makes Scams Harder To Spot

New Toyota RAV4 Has A Comfort Issue Some Owners Can't Ignore

Used EVs Are Selling Faster Than Gas Cars, but Tesla Isn't Leading

Range-extended EVs are the awkward middle child between hybrids and full-on electrics. They roll around on electric motors, but there’s still a gasoline engine lurking in the background, acting as a generator when the battery needs a top-up. The idea is you get to cruise on electric power without sweating over where the next charging station is hiding.

But keeping a combustion engine onboard means you still get the usual suspects: noise and vibrations. Even if the engine isn’t hooked up to the wheels, it can still send a droning soundtrack straight into the cabin.

Porsche, never one to shy away from a technical puzzle, seems to have a workaround in mind. A patent that just surfaced shows a setup with both an electric motor and a combustion engine. The twist? Porsche wants to stick a two-cylinder boxer engine in the back as the range extender.

The patent was first discovered by CarMoses. Here’s where things get clever: instead of just piling on more insulation or fancy engine mounts, Porsche wants to use the electric motor itself to fight back against the unwanted engine noise and vibrations.

Think of it like noise-canceling headphones, but for your car. The system listens for the engine’s racket and then tells the electric motor to make just the right counter-move, tackling both the noise and the shakes that sneak through the car’s bones.

The setup involves a sound sensor in the cabin and a movement sensor near the engine, both feeding data to a control unit that decides how the electric motor should fight back against the noise.

Porsche even wants to preload the system with data about engine RPM and other conditions, so it knows exactly how to respond. If that’s not enough, they might throw in a shaker or a speaker to help quiet things down even more.

Unlike regular noise-canceling setups, here the electric motor pulls double duty as part of the noise-fighting team. In some cases, that means you won’t even need a separate gadget just to handle the counter-noise.

One possible application is a range-extended electric vehicle in which the combustion engine runs a generator instead of mechanically driving the wheels. Since the engine can operate at a relatively consistent speed, its noise characteristics could be easier for the system to anticipate and counteract.

That could mean less of the dreaded drone during long trips, when the gas engine has to keep chugging away to feed the battery. It also means a quieter, more refined cabin without loading up on extra soundproofing or complicated hardware. Letting the electric motor multitask could be a smart way to keep things simple.

For now, however, Porsche hasn’t announced a production vehicle featuring this technology. The patent also doesn’t establish whether the company intends to use the proposed arrangement in a future model or whether it is simply exploring the engineering possibilities.

As with other patent filings, the application and its publication do not guarantee that the technology will reach production. Automakers regularly patent ideas that may never make it beyond the development stage. All trademarks and brand names mentioned belong to their respective owners.

Toyota is giving its best-selling Corolla a major makeover, and an all-electric version is part of the plan. The upcoming Corolla Cross EV was captured in public for the first time ahead of its expected 2027 debut.

The Corolla has always been “a car for everyone,” Toyota’s former president and current CEO, Koji Sato, said after unveiling the next-gen Corolla Concept at last year’s Japan Mobility Show.

Since it went on sale 60 years ago, over 57 million drivers have chosen the Corolla, making it Toyota’s best-selling vehicle ever.

The Corolla has undergone 12 model changes since 1966, but the compact car is about to undergo its biggest transformation yet.

Although it’s still a top seller, the Corolla has lost some of its appeal as new, more advanced, and efficient options have emerged. Toyota looks to change that with the next-generation model.

It will remain “a car for everyone,” as Sato said, but the next-gen Corolla will come in multiple powertrains, including an all-electric version.

“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle―whatever the power source―let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive,” Sato said at the Japan Mobility Show last October.

Ahead of its expected debut sometime in 2027, a disguised Corolla Cross EV was spotted driving near Toyota’s European headquarters and R&D center.

New images from Chinese media outlet Autohome show what’s expected to be the all-electric Corolla Cross, with a closed-off grille and a unique body design.

The new Corolla will be the first to use Toyota’s new “multipathway” platform that will support electric, hybrid, gas, and other powertrains.

Toyota hasn’t revealed specifics, including battery or powertrain specs, but the next-gen Corolla EV is expected to remain close in style to the Concept. Aside from the massive COROLLA badge on the back, it looks like an entirely different vehicle with a near sports-car-like silhouette.

In an exclusive interview with Japanese media NHK in July, Toyota’s current chairman and former CEO, Akio Toyoda, warned that the company “cannot survive” if it does not adapt amid new competition and technology from China.

During the special, which went behind the scenes at Toyota’s “top secret” development site, several blurred Corolla Concept body types, including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and GR model, were revealed in the background.

According to a recent Nikkei report, Toyota plans to begin production of the next-gen Corolla in 2028 through its joint venture with Chinese state-owned FAW Group, FAW Toyota Motor.

The Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations with a driving range of at least 250 miles.

The hybrid version will reportedly use a new 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.

Toyota has yet to confirm the electric version will launch in the US. According to Car and Driver, the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.

#4406. Tesla Powerwall 3 now boosts heat pumps to store cheap solar as heat

Tesla has launched Heat Pump Optimization, a feature that lets the Powerwall 3 and three-phase Powerwall 3P tell a compatible heat pump when to run harder so a home can bank cheap or surplus solar energy as hot water.

It’s live in Europe only. Tesla hasn’t said anything about bringing it to the US or Canada, and the hardware standard it relies on barely exists on this side of the Atlantic.

According to Tesla’s support page for the feature, the Powerwall watches electricity prices and solar production throughout the day and sends the heat pump one of two signals: run normally, or boost.

When it’s told to boost, the heat pump heats water beyond what the home needs right now, typically into a domestic hot water or buffer tank. That stored heat then carries the house through the expensive hours, when the heat pump can run less.

What triggers a boost depends on the Powerwall’s operating mode:

Tesla Energy summed it up on X last week: “Heat Pump Optimization allows your Powerwall to boost heating when there’s surplus solar or energy is inexpensive.”

There’s no cloud integration with heat pump brands here. It’s a wire.

The feature runs on SG-Ready (Smart Grid Ready), a label the German Heat Pump Association (BWP) introduced back in 2012 with 17 manufacturers. It uses two relay contacts on the heat pump to signal four operating states, from a utility block to a forced switch-on. Tesla only uses the “normal” and “boosted” recommendations.

Tesla’s requirements are pretty specific:

And there are limits. The signals are only recommendations, so the heat pump’s own thermostat settings can override them. Tesla also notes each signal has to be held for at least 10 minutes to comply with SG-Ready, and the feature drops back to normal during a power outage so the Powerwall can prioritize backup loads.

Oddly, there’s no on/off toggle in the Tesla app. Once it’s wired up, it’s on.

The math is what makes this interesting. A 300-liter hot water tank heated an extra 30°C holds about 10.5 kWh of thermal energy. With a heat pump running at a COP of 3, that takes only around 3.5 kWh of electricity to store.

So a tank most European heat pump homes already have can soak up a big chunk of midday solar without touching the lithium in the garage. That leaves the Powerwall’s 13.5 kWh free for the stuff that can’t be stored as heat.

The market is there too. Germany sold 299,000 heating heat pumps in 2025, up 55% year-over-year according to BWP, and they made up nearly half of all new heating systems sold in the country for the first time.

Tesla is also late to this. sonnen pushed a software update in 2023 that lets its sonnenBatterie run heat pumps off surplus solar, starting with NIBE units, and SG-Ready control has been a standard feature of German PV energy managers for years.

watches electricity prices and solar production throughout the day and sends the heat pump one of two signals: run normally, or boost.

Heatpumps over here have been able to do this for years already.

And it's not one of two signals. Inverter controlled HP's enables control if the effect, and not just "normal or boost".

It’s the latest Europe-first move for Tesla Energy after it launched the Powerwall 3P with a native three-phase inverter earlier this year, aimed squarely at Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. The company announced its 1 millionth Powerwall last year, and software like this is how it squeezes more value out of that installed base.

This is a smart, cheap feature, and it’s exactly the kind of thing that makes a home battery more valuable without adding a single cell.

Heat is the biggest energy load in most homes in cold climates, and water is about the cheapest storage medium there is. Using a battery’s brain to time the heat pump around solar and tariffs makes a lot more sense than discharging lithium to run a compressor at 6 p.m.

Home batteries are changing the economics of residential energy, and pairing them with solar (and smart loads like heat pumps) is the best way to get the most out of them. The engine in question came from a 2021 Lincoln Aviator with approximately 70,000 miles on the odometer.

New Toyota RAV4 Has A Comfort Issue Some Owners Can't Ignore

Ford’s 3.0-liter EcoBoost V6 is known for its V8-like low-end torque, and some of the brand’s performance models, such as the Explorer ST and Ranger Raptor, use it. The engine can be fairly robust, but with poor maintenance, even a dependable power unit is bound to suffer.

Case in point: This EcoBoost V6 from a 2021 Lincoln Aviator, the luxury counterpart of the Ford Explorer, failed and was acquired by Eric of I Do Cars as a core return. The engine reportedly received only two or three oil changes despite having already clocked about 70,000 miles. At that mileage, it should have undergone at least seven oil changes, based on Ford’s maximum recommended interval of 10,000 miles.

From the outside, the engine looked intact, which was fortunate, as inadequate lubrication can cause excessive friction, overheating, and potentially catastrophic engine failure. But on the inside, the valvetrain and chain-driven timing system looked grim, with an abundance of oil varnish and sludge. It looked far more worn out than expected for a five-year-old engine.

Given that the 3.0-liter EcoBoost V6 uses direct injection rather than the dual-injection setup found in the 2.7-liter version, the intake valves had significant carbon buildup. For the uninitiated, a dual-injection setup also sprays fuel into the intake ports, helping clean carbon deposits from the intake valves.

Moving to the engine block, the cylinders showed signs of moisture, likely because the engine had been sitting outside. Debris circulating in the contaminated oil likely contributed to significant damage to the engine’s internal bearings. The failure culminated in a spun rod bearing on cylinder six, with bearing shavings also found in the oil pan.

With the EcoBoost V6 using a twin-turbocharger setup, it is more demanding to maintain than a naturally aspirated counterpart. Such a setup operates under greater thermal and mechanical stress, making proper lubrication and cooling crucial to getting the most out of its performance. After all, the cost of maintaining a luxury vehicle like a Lincoln should be part of the ownership equation in the first place.

The 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged EcoBoost V6 remains in use today, with Lincoln rating the 2027 Aviator at 400 horsepower and 415 lb-ft of torque. The Aviator was previously available as a plug-in hybrid, which made 494 hp and 630 lb-ft of torque, but was discontinued for the 2024 model year.

#4401. Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

Vince Zampella, co-creator of Call of Duty, and a veteran studio head responsible for some of the biggest franchises in the world, is gone.

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”

Inside the Bureau of Customs compound at Manila Harbor, a substantial collection of confiscated exotic vehicles is awaiting public auction. Authorities seized the fleet from operators of illegal offshore gambling networks who attempted to import the vehicles into the Philippines without paying the required duties. The most prominent models currently held in the government yard include a 2021 McLaren Senna and a rare Ferrari LaFerrari hybrid hypercar.

While we frequently see domestic police seize cars from local street racing syndicates, the financial scale of the Manila impound lot is distinctly different. The Philippine government imposes a 100 percent luxury tax on European automotive imports, which prompted the illicit operators to bypass customs entirely. With the gambling networks now shut down by authorities, the abandoned high-performance vehicles are slated for auction to recover the lost tax revenue.

According to a video from the amadeusiom YouTube channel, the auction inventory features several high-value European models. Beyond the McLaren Senna, which carries an estimated auction floor price of $1.01 million, the impound lot holds a 2022 Ferrari SF90 Stradale, a Rolls-Royce Cullinan, a Bentley Continental GT, and a Rolls-Royce Phantom. Because the vehicles have been parked outdoors in a humid, tropical climate, several models will require significant cosmetic rehabilitation before returning to the road.

Stateside, exotic vehicles occasionally cross the auction block after federal agents seize assets from high-profile financial fugitives. However, the Philippine customs bureau faces a unique challenge in officially valuing its rarest capture: the LaFerrari. Because the limited-production hybrid is exceptionally scarce on the global market, officials are struggling to establish a realistic reserve price that accurately incorporates the mandatory 100 percent import tax, leaving the Ferrari in a temporary regulatory holding pattern.

While domestic buyers frequently monitor government surplus websites hoping to score seized cars cheap at public sales, the upcoming Manila auction operates under strict financial parameters. The government’s mandatory reserve prices must account for local market values and the heavy import taxation rate. Consequently, the asking prices remain high by international standards, with a 2022 Rolls-Royce Phantom carrying a floor price of over $380,000 despite its current storage conditions.

Despite the high financial barriers to entry, the Bureau of Customs is proceeding with the sealed-bid public auction to convert these assets into usable government funds. However, the state has historically taken a much harsher stance on smuggling. In previous years, the Philippine government made global headlines by publicly crushing seized exotics with bulldozers as a strict warning to tax evaders. While this specific hypercar fleet was ultimately spared the crusher to benefit local taxpayers, the logistics of selling million-dollar vehicles directly from a port highlight the complex realities of international customs enforcement.

#4399. An Uncompromising Fraternal Twin: We Drive the All-Electric 2027 BMW i3

It may not look all that different, but the electric i3 sedan differs from its 3-series siblings in a few key ways.

While BMW’s latest i3 may look like a carbon copy of its gas-powered 3-series sibling, using the gasser to underpin the EV would incur all manner of compromise. BMW did this with its i4 and the 430i models, and the concessions are obvious. In order to get a battery-electric powertrain tucked in the 430i’s body, BMW had to limit the battery size while using air springs to manage the car’s newfound mass. BMW wasn’t willing to make those sacrifices for its electric 3, and as a result, the i3 is actually quite different from its internal-combustion sibling.

The Munich-built BMW i3 50 xDrive sedan shares nothing with the new Dingolfing-made M350 and 330 models, except the front grille, the mirror housings, and possibly the door handles. Everything else is different, and that is reflected by a 1.5-inch stretch in wheelbase, plus some extra height and width. The length, on the other hand, differs only by a few hairs. But the difference is so much more than numbers on a page. Without having to worry about fitting an inline-six under the hood, the i3’s cabin is pushed forward, and the windshield glass picks up some extra rake. The Neue Klasse styling applied to both cars is effective at hiding these differences, but keen eyes may still pick up on the slightly steeper hood and the shorter front-wheel-to-door-edge gap.

See all results for new 2027 BMW i3 for sale near 29405

Adjusting the wheelbase and vehicle height was necessary to fit the electric drivetrain BMW wanted in there, and as a result, we think the i3 50 xDrive outshines the i4. The prime mover is a current-excited synchronous rear motor making 322 horsepower and 321 pound-feet of torque, the same kind of e-motor in the i4. However, the i3’s front motor has been changed to a 165-hp, 188-lb-ft induction motor, and that alteration makes it more efficient because there is less drag when it isn’t engaged. It’s more efficient at speed too. Accounting for the usual fuzzy EV-motor math, the i3 50’s full output is a meaty 463 horses and 476 pound-feet, enough to push the electric 3 to 60 mph in an estimated 4.2 seconds.

Also unlike the i4, the i3’s battery is not a limit in any way, shape, or form. It’s much more capacious, toting 112 kWh instead of the i4’s 84 kWh. We estimate the range at a fantastic 450 miles (the EPA has yet to rate it), which is a bit higher than BMW’s own number, since the electric iX3 SUV’s official range also surpassed BMW’s initial internal figure. The two vehicles share a powertrain, so we figure the powertrain’s overachieving nature will transfer from SUV to sedan too. On the charging front, the pack’s 800-volt architecture means it can gulp down electricity at 400 kilowatts (if you can find a charger that can support it). A NACS port is standard equipment, with an included adapter for SAE Combo charging.

See all results for new 2027 BMW i3 for sale near 29405

Despite leaving the optional M adaptive dampers at home, the car we drove seemed expertly tuned, with a ride that was taut but never too firm. The battery’s low mass helped keep the car feeling planted in corners, with just enough roll stiffness to keep body lean disciplined without introducing harshness or head toss to upset the proceedings.

And we pushed it hard in corners, too. Some of this feeling comes from BMW’s “Heart of Joy” computer, which sorts out the steering, friction braking, regenerative braking, throttle inputs, and more—in a claimed one-tenth of the time that previous BMW software stacks required. Brake-based rear differential action, something we usually don’t care for, was silky smooth in this system and felt for all the world like an electronically controlled rear diff. Brake response is uncommonly good, and there is enough regenerative braking capacity that nearly all your routine stops will be handled magnetically.

The one thing we were less effervescent about was the steering feel. The i3’s helm is certainly accurate and direct enough, but it doesn’t quite have the feel and feedback of the gas-powered M350 we drove (and reviewed separately). Perhaps that differentiator is there intentionally; after all, there’s a sportier i3 M60 model coming.

At least the i3 we drove didn’t have the dorky steering wheel with odd vertical spokes. (The optional M Sport wheel puts said spokes in a vastly more normal location.) BMW’s trick Panoramic Vision screen works even better in the i3 than it does in the M350, because the dash-spanning display strip is more visible above the wheel, yet it doesn’t hide the road. The taller but more steeply angled hood works in its favor, for sure. The central touchscreen is the same 17.9-inch display found in the M350 and has all the same characteristics. On the positive side, it looks great, and the angled shape is quite natural. On the other hand, let’s just say that vent aiming is better done manually, rather than via touchscreen controls, and there are other functions that could benefit from a real button or two. You can save a few bucks by not opting for the head-up display, which seems redundant when you already have a wealth of information at the base of the windscreen.

We also like the i3’s soaring panoramic glass roof, which provides an abundance of headroom. Rear-seat space is slightly larger than the M350’s, but toe space beneath the front seat can be tighter if the front occupant has their chair lowered to the floor. BMW doesn’t have a U.S.-specific figure for trunk space just yet, but preliminary German figures place its 15 cubic feet just one cube in arrears of the M350 gasser.

The BMW i3 50 xDrive will launch in the first quarter of 2027, right alongside the gas-powered 3-series lineup. It starts at $62,850, which seems like a great deal for all you get. The i3 feels mighty special and has the potential to draw new buyers into the electric fold. It’s got gobs of range, it charges fast, and it delivers speed and poise like a proper BMW.

#4398. Hardee’s gets EV fast charging – with Carl’s Jr. locations to follow

EV drivers have a new reason to pull into Hardee’s. Energized EV has opened four fast-charging ports at a restaurant in Temple, Georgia, kicking off a planned rollout at Hardee’s and Carl’s Jr. locations across the US.

There’s no site count or rollout schedule yet, but the first location is open with both NACS and CCS1 connectors.

The chargers are at 587 Carrollton Street in Temple. The site has two dual-port XCharge C7 DC fast chargers, each rated at 240 kW, for a total of four charging ports. Monta provides the chargers’ software. XCharge says the C7 adjusts power output between its two connectors, and both NACS and CCS1 connectors are on offer.

“Adding charging at our restaurants gives EV drivers a convenient place to stop, recharge, and enjoy a meal,” said Mike Darger, vice president of facilities and maintenance at CKE Restaurants. “We look forward to building on this first opening as more locations come online across the country.”

Energized EV says more Hardee’s and Carl’s Jr. sites are planned across the US, with president and CEO Devin Grandis calling Temple “the beginning of a much larger expansion.”

Energy & Environmental Design Services LLC (E&EDS) is the program’s exclusive installer. Its services include charging infrastructure design, installation, and maintenance, as well as electrical contracting.

Energized EV’s approach is to install chargers where drivers already stop, whether they’re running errands or taking a longer road trip. But we’ll need the next locations and opening dates to see how useful this restaurant charging network will become. The announcement doesn’t list charging prices for Temple.

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The update is also adding some important new features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the new Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock new second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two new main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Toyota GR86 owners with the Brembo package will need to prepare a small fortune for replacement pads at the dealer.

Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push

I know there is a price for performance, but the prices that Toyota charges for performance brake pads are kind of ridiculous, borderline extortionate. In case you didn’t know, there is an OEM performance package that some special GR86s come standard with, and customers can opt into their deal when purchasing their vehicle brand new.

The performance package includes Sachs dampers and a Brembo big brake kit and costs as much as $2,020 on the base trim and $1,500 on the premium trim. That sounds like a great deal until you run out of brake pads. Remember this number because it will come in handy later.

While the performance package is already a steal of a deal from Toyota, the money that it will take to sustain that performance is something else. In a video posted by JamiesGarage1 (@JamiesGarage1 on YouTube), he found out through a customer’s GR86 with the performance package that Toyota charges ridiculous prices for Brembo brake pads and rotors.

How much, you ask? Well, for the front pads alone, the suggested retail price is $1,481.44. For the front brake rotors, each Brembo unit costs $521.25; multiplying that by two, we get $1,042.50, bringing the total for the parts alone to $2,523.94. Adding the rear brakes into the mix, the rear pads are $1,380, and each rear brake rotor is at a mind-boggling $562.20 per piece.

If, for some reason, your GR86 needed all four corners to get a rotor and a pad replaced all at once, you’ll be set back a total of $5,028.34, which is more than triple the price of the performance package from the configurator, and that doesn’t even include tax and labor costs. JamiesGarage mentioned those prices are retail, and shops can get these parts at a discount, but we’re still looking at a total close to $4,000. Like I said, ridiculous.

After watching the video, we decided to check online prices for the pads. It’s important to note that non-Brembo models will cost about a hundred dollars for either the front or the rear; however, the Brembo sets will still set you back about $992.16 for the front and $924.09 for the rear, as seen on Toyota Parts Deal. That’s more “reasonable,” but it also goes to show just how much of a steal the Toyota GR86’s performance package really is.

JamiesGarage even went on to recount his experiences in a Mercedes dealership when it came time to replace a Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren’s brakes. The total bill was estimated to be around $40,000, but that’s a car that costs over $500,000. That car’s brakes cost just as much as a whole GR86, and customers will be paying around 14% of its retail value to maintain the brakes.

On that note, it’s also important to know that Toyota doesn’t use high-end calipers either; instead, they’re four-piston fixed calipers paired with a 12.8-inch rotor in the front and painted red, while the rear is given two-piston calipers paired with a 12.4-inch rotor. No carbon ceramics to speak of here, just a normal Brembo system that’s similar to the old Subaru WRX STI or BRZ’s setup.

Alternatively, you can get aftermarket pads and rotors. A trip to the GR86.org forum and you’ll find that some owners have already hunted down some alternatives and given their recommendations. Though keep in mind that your vehicle’s warranty might be called into question.

#4395. The BMW iX is sold out, but you might like what takes its place even more

BMW is saying goodbye to the iX. With the 2026 model essentially sold out, BMW is preparing to introduce its replacement, which already looks like a big upgrade.

The iX went on sale in the US in 2022 as BMW’s first dedicated electric SUV. After a short four-year run, BMW confirmed earlier this year that it was discontinuing the iX in the US after the 2026 model year to make room for its next-generation of fully electric vehicles.

BMW didn’t take long to sell through inventory, with 2026 iX models essentially sold out in the US.

The iX landing page now redirects you to the new BMW X5 instead. According to online auto research firm CarsDirect, about 10 new iX models remain nationwide.

BMW’s Neue Klasse vehicles, starting with the new 2027 iX3, mark a step change from its previous EVs.

At the center is the Neue Klasse platform, which introduces BMW’s sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive, new batteries, and an 800-volt electrical architecture.

BMW said the new Gen6 eDrive system delivers 30% higher charging speeds and driving range than its previous system, with some models seeing an even greater increase.

The 2027 iX3 50 xDrive, BMW’s first Neue Klasse vehicle, starts at $61,500 and offers an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 434 miles. In comparison, the 2026 iX xDrive 60 had an EPA range of up to 364 miles.

While the iX3 is a smaller, compact electric SUV compared to the iX, BMW is preparing to launch the iX5 as a more direct replacement.

The gas-powered 2027 X5 40 xDrive is now on sale, starting at $72,100, but BMW is expected to launch the electric iX5 in early 2027.

A few weeks ago, BMW put the new iX5 60 xDrive to the test at an international media event in Southern California to show just how fast it can charge.

During the event, the new iX5 hit a peak of 464 kW. BMW said that with up to 460 kW peak charging, the iX5 60 xDrive can add up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes. To charge the battery from 10% to 80% takes just 22 minutes.

Using a 144 kWh battery, BMW said the electric SUV will offer up to an estimated 435 miles of range on a single charge.

The iX5 is powered by a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain, delivering a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque. BMW says it can go from 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds and tow up to 6,000 lbs.

Inside, the iX5 will be an upgrade from the iX, adopting BMW’s Neue Klasse design. The setup includes a 17.9″ navigation touchscreen and the new BMW Panoramic Vision that spans the windshield. You can also opt to add the optional 14.6″ passenger screen for a third display.

Measuring 197.2″ long, 78.7″ wide, and 68.9″ tall, the iX5 is slightly longer and taller than the outgoing iX, with more of a traditional SUV design.

BMW is expected to open orders for the new iX5 60 xDrive this month, starting at $79,800, with a full launch in early 2027. It will be BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US.

Production is set to begin at BMW’s Plant Spartanburg in South Carolina by the end of the year, with the first deliveries expected in early 2027.

#4393. Why Chinese Cars Are Packed With Features Americans Don't Always Ask For

Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push

Car Loan Fraud Is Costing Billions As AI Makes Scams Harder To Spot

New Toyota RAV4 Has A Comfort Issue Some Owners Can't Ignore

Why do some Chinese cars come loaded with technology while American vehicles often put affordability first? A recent study offers an interesting explanation.

Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push

Car Loan Fraud Is Costing Billions As AI Makes Scams Harder To Spot

New Toyota RAV4 Has A Comfort Issue Some Owners Can't Ignore

Used EVs Are Selling Faster Than Gas Cars, but Tesla Isn't Leading

What do you first consider when buying a car? Is it the price, the technology included, or perhaps the safety features? It turns out that the answer varies considerably depending on where you live. A recent study by Bain & Company highlights a noticeable difference between the buying priorities of American and Chinese consumers, offering some insight into why vehicles from these two markets can be so different.

Bain’s 2026 Global Auto Consumer Survey polled over 12,000 car shoppers around the globe. The big takeaway? What people care about most when picking out a car isn’t the same everywhere.

For Americans, price is king – 68% say it’s their number one concern. Europeans aren’t far behind at 62%. But in China, it’s a whole different ballgame: 58% of buyers put technology and features at the top of their wish list.

It’s not exactly shocking when you look at the bigger picture. With living costs climbing in the US and Europe, keeping things affordable is a must. Meanwhile, Chinese automakers are locked in a price war, so cars there are cheaper – and that leaves plenty of room to pack in extra tech as a selling point.

These preferences help explain why Chinese automakers have become particularly generous when it comes to technology and equipment. It’s not unusual for vehicles from Chinese brands to come with large infotainment displays, multiple digital interfaces, advanced driver assistance systems, and comfort features that would otherwise be optional extras elsewhere.

In China, where buyers are tech-hungry, automakers are in a full-on features arms race. If it plugs in, lights up, or talks back, it’s probably in there – everything but the kitchen sink.

American automakers, meanwhile, still have to pay close attention to pricing, particularly in the mass-market segment. That doesn’t mean American buyers don’t appreciate technology. In fact, 49% of US respondents still ranked technology and features among their top considerations.

Brand loyalty is another interesting difference. According to Bain, 79% of American mass-market buyers and 72% of premium buyers considered only established brands during their previous purchase. In China, brand loyalty is considerably weaker, with 24% of respondents saying they don’t care about the brand at all.

Regional differences aren’t the only factor shaping the automotive market. Age also plays a considerable role, particularly when it comes to electric vehicles.

Bain’s findings show that younger buyers are generally more receptive to battery electric vehicles (BEVs). Around 50% of Gen Y and Gen Z consumers in the US and China are open to purchasing one. In Europe, the figure reaches 46% for younger buyers.

Older buyers? Not so much. Just 22% of older Americans are willing to go electric, compared to 50% of the younger crowd. China bucks the trend, though – over half of all age groups there are open to EVs.

So, what does this mean? Car companies can’t make the same model for everyone and expect it to work. What excites a young Chinese buyer might not interest an older American. For global brands, understanding these differences is as important as creating new car technology.

#4392. bp pulse makes 850+ EV fast chargers easier to use in the US

EV drivers have another way to charge at bp pulse without adding its app to their phones. The network has joined ChargeHub’s Passport Hub, connecting more than 850 charging points at over 95 US locations to ChargeHub and participating charging services and automakers.

Drivers can find, access, and pay for bp pulse charging through ChargeHub or participating services connected to Passport Hub.

Passport Hub handles the connections between charging networks and the services drivers use, including exchanging session information and settling payments. That lets a charging operator connect to multiple services through a single integration.

In practice, ChargeHub users can pull up a bp pulse location, select a port, and start charging from their existing account. The app displays the charging cost and wallet balance, and drivers need funds in their ChargeHub wallet to begin charging.

ChargeHub also shows real-time charger availability and lets drivers filter by connector type. Its bp pulse guide says most of the network’s chargers use CCS, with a growing share offering NACS.

Meanwhile, bp pulse has been adding physical charging sites, too. Recent openings include 12 charging bays at a TravelCenters of America location in Grand Bay, Alabama, and 22 bays near Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport.

Before starting a session, check the price shown in the app. ChargeHub’s guide notes that its Plus subscription waives activation fees, so using an existing account doesn’t necessarily mean paying the same total as another payment method.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

One-off creations can offer several benefits for automakers. For one, they can strengthen a brand’s identity and generate interest, something Bugatti knows well with exclusive hypercars like the Brouillard. Another potential benefit is profitability, as automakers can charge a premium for bespoke vehicles without committing to full-scale production. These creations also cater to the specific demands of clients who typically have exceptionally deep pockets.

Karma Automotive has a new entry into the one-off vehicle space with the Eximius 1. Unveiled at the Concours at Wynn Las Vegas, the Eximius 1 is the first creation under Karma’s new bespoke vehicle program, similar to Porsche’s Sonderwunsch and Rolls-Royce’s Coachbuild. However, the company’s approach is particularly notable because it allows extensive powertrain modifications, not just unique paintwork, body panels, and interiors. For this particular build, the vehicle features a 6.2-liter V8 serving as a generator in a plug-in series hybrid system, a significant departure from the 1.5-liter turbocharged three-cylinder engine used in the Revero donor car.

The Revero is Karma’s outgoing model as it prepares to introduce four new electrified models over the coming years. As such, the Eximius 1 can be seen as a loud send-off following the Revero’s long run dating back to 2016, when it evolved from the Fisker Karma, a luxury plug-in hybrid sedan that fell victim to its manufacturer’s financial collapse.

Karma claims that the track-focused Eximius 1 will produce nearly 1,200 horsepower, attributing 550 hp to the V8 generator and 645 hp to the battery. With that much power on paper, the automaker claims the vehicle will be the most powerful plug-in series hybrid ever developed. It is expected to sprint from zero to 60 mph in 2.7 seconds and reach an estimated top speed of over 200 mph. Other performance bits include 21-inch center-lock magnesium wheels, carbon-ceramic brakes with two-piece slotted brake rotors, and Öhlins semi-active suspension.

Finished in Borealis Blue, the one-off vehicle does look like a more aggressive version of the Revero, with modifications like extensive carbon-fiber construction, bodywork that’s 50 mm (1.97 inches) wider, a front splitter, air intakes, and a large rear wing. The cabin, meanwhile, features Recaro carbon-fiber front bucket seats, a simplified carbon-fiber center console with an emergency kill switch, and a specially fitted carbon-fiber racing helmet displayed between the rear seats.

No pricing was disclosed, though Karma said that the Eximius 1 will be delivered to an unnamed customer in 2027.

While the customer gets to drive a vehicle that cannot be found elsewhere, Karma will start to roll out its revitalized series-production lineup, starting with the Gyesera plug-in series hybrid in December 2026. The Amaris GT two-door plug-in series hybrid will arrive in Q4 2027, followed by two EVs, namely the Kaveya, arriving in Q1 2028, and the Ivara, which will follow later. The Kaveya is also planned to use solid-state battery technology.

#4388. Shaquille O’Neal Bought This 2004 Rolls-Royce Phantom Just to Prove a Point

It’s now for sale on Bring a Trailer. Maybe you’ve got something to prove?

One of the greatest basketball players of all time, four-time NBA champion Shaquille O’Neal was one of the most formidable centers in the game. That doesn’t mean he never got outplayed.

To hear him tell the story, during his stint playing for the Lakers, he wandered into a Rolls-Royce dealership dressed casually in sweats. In his words, “I like to spend money, but I don’t like to waste money. I don’t want to spend $400,000 for a car.” Thus, every time the salesman tells him the price for a particular Roller, O'Neal waves him off.

Finally, the salesman asks, “You’re asking about all these cars—can you afford them?” Riled up, Shaq buys three Rolls-Royces on the spot. Heck of a flex by the NBA player, but not a bad move by the salesman, who gets to pocket a triple-Rolls commission.

See all results for used cars for sale near 74107

One of that trio of Rolls-Royces just turned up at Bring a Trailer (which, like Car and Driver, is part of Hearst Autos): a 2004 Phantom sedan in glossy silver. Yes, the driver’s seat goes back, way back, but this Roller is going to set you back far less than O’Neal’s impulse purchase.

This was the debut model year for the Phantom VII, the first Rolls-Royce of the BMW ownership era. Like Shaq, much of this generation of Rolls-Royce’s curb presence comes from its sheer size; the sedan was longer than a Ford Excursion when it launched.

Power came from an enlarged version of the BMW 750’s V-12, here displacing 6.75 liters. Peak power was 453 horsepower, but a more subtle motivating force was the 531 pound-feet of torque. Almost 400 pound-feet was available from just 1000 rpm, fed through a smooth-shifting six-speed automatic, giving the Phantom a driving experience less like a luxury sedan and more like a Cunard cruise liner.

Add in coach doors with integrated umbrellas, self-righting Rolls-Royce center-caps on the wheels, and a retractable Spirit of Ecstasy on the massive hood, and this generation of Phantom is plenty imposing. It’s even better on the inside, with acres of walnut trim, buttery leather, and deep-pile lambswool carpets. Other faintly ridiculous amenities include rear picnic tables and six-zone climate control.

Shaq says he barely drove his three Rolls-Royces, although this example now has 45K miles on the odometer. That means there’s still plenty of luxurious life ahead, along with a great story about the day somebody scored on Shaquille O’Neal.

Pagani’s birthday bash just got its final guest, as the third special Huayra rolls out for everyone to see.

Karma Reveals a 1,200-HP V8 Hybrid Built for Just One Buyer

Why Chinese Cars Are Packed With Features Americans Don't Always Ask For

Pagani has completed its Huayra 70 trilogy by revealing the Huayra 70 Anima. This unique car joins the other two special editions, marking the end of the founder’s 70th birthday celebration. For fans of manual transmissions, this model includes one as well.

The Huayra 70 series began with the Trionfo, built by Pagani’s Grandi Complicazioni team. Next up was the Huayra 70 Derecho, which showed off at Goodwood earlier this year. This one mixed Pearl Orange with deep Inky Blue for maximum visual drama. But the real headline was under the hood: an 864-horsepower twin-turbo V12 and a seven-speed manual.

Now, the trilogy is complete. Pagani just dropped the Huayra 70 Anima at the Wynn Las Vegas Concours, giving us one last, very different take on the Huayra formula. ‘Anima’ means soul in Italian, and this one definitely has its own vibe.

The Anima stands out with deep metallic blue paint, exposed carbon fiber, and just enough silver and light-blue accents to keep things interesting. It’s an open-top, with sculpted bodywork wrapping the cockpit and roll hoops that look ready for anything.

Up front, the Anima sports a low nose, gaping air intakes, and a splitter that means business. The sides show off wild aero, beefy rear haunches, and a rear wing that refuses to be ignored. Out back, there’s more exposed carbon, an angry diffuser, and a six-pipe exhaust setup that looks ready to wake the neighbors.

Inside, it’s a blue-and-white affair. White leather wraps the seats and most of the cockpit, with blue accents popping up everywhere. Exposed machined aluminum is scattered across the dash, steering wheel, and center console. As always, Pagani’s switchgear is a work of art – every piece looks like it belongs in a jewelry case.

The Anima keeps it old-school with three pedals and a manual shifter, complete with exposed linkage so you can watch the mechanical magic happen. The gear lever matches the blue-and-white theme, and a plaque reminds you this is number 3 of 3 – so don’t expect to see another one at Cars and Coffee.

Pagani’s keeping the Anima’s full specs under wraps for now, but it’s likely packing the same Mercedes-AMG 6.0-liter twin-turbo V12 as the Derecho. That means 864 hp, 811 pound-feet of torque, and all of it going to the rear wheels through a seven-speed manual. We’ll update when Pagani spills more details.

Like its siblings, the Huayra 70 Anima is a one-off, not something you’ll see at your local dealership. Pagani’s Grandi Complicazioni team handled the build, as usual for these ultra-bespoke projects.

No official price yet, but with all the custom work, rare materials, and one-of-one status, you can bet the sticker shock will be real. As for availability, this one’s spoken for, and with Anima rounding out the Huayra 70 trio, don’t expect any more to pop up with this badge.
